rows.en: True eccentrics never deliberately set out to draw attention to themselves.
rows.zh: 真正的怪人从不会刻意设法引人注意。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They disregard social conventions without being conscious that they are doing anything extraordinary.
rows.zh: 他们不理会社会习俗，却并不觉得自己的举动有什么出格。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This invariably wins them the love and respect of others, for they add colour to the dull routine of everyday life.
rows.zh: 这总能为他们赢来别人的喜爱和尊重，因为他们给单调的日常生活增添了色彩。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Up to the time of his death, Richard Colson was one of the most notable figures in our town.
rows.zh: 理查德·科尔森一直到去世时，都是我们镇上最出名的人物之一。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He was a shrewd and wealthy businessman, but most people in the town hardly knew anything about this side of his life.
rows.zh: 他是个精明而富有的商人，但镇上大多数人对他生活的这一面几乎一无所知。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He was known to us all as Dickie and his eccentricity had become legendary long before he died.
rows.zh: 大家都叫他迪基；早在他去世以前，他的种种怪癖就已成了传奇。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Dickie disliked snobs intensely.
rows.zh: 迪基极其讨厌势利眼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though he owned a large car, he hardly ever used it, preferring always to go on foot.
rows.zh: 他虽然有一辆大汽车，却几乎从来不用，总爱步行出门。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even when it was raining heavily, he refused to carry an umbrella.
rows.zh: 即使下着大雨，他也不肯带伞。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One day, he walked into an expensive shop after having been caught in a particularly heavy shower.
rows.zh: 一天，他被一场特别猛烈的阵雨淋了个透，随后走进了一家高档商店。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He wanted to buy a £300 watch for his wife, but he was in such a bedraggled condition that an assistant refused to serve him.
rows.zh: 他想给妻子买一块价值三百英镑的手表，可他浑身湿透、狼狈不堪，一个店员竟不肯接待他。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Dickie left the shop without a word and returned carrying a large cloth bag.
rows.zh: 迪基一声不吭地离开商店，又提着一只大布袋回来了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As it was extremely heavy, he dumped it on the counter.
rows.zh: 袋子重极了，他把它重重地放在柜台上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The assistant asked him to leave, but Dickie paid no attention to him and requested to see the manager.
rows.zh: 店员叫他出去，迪基却毫不理睬，要求见经理。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Recognizing who the customer was, the manager was most apologetic and reprimanded the assistant severely.
rows.zh: 经理认出了这位顾客是谁，连忙赔不是，并狠狠训斥了那个店员。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When Dickie was given the watch, he presented the assistant with the cloth bag.
rows.zh: 拿到手表以后，迪基把布袋递给了店员。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It contained £300 in pennies.
rows.zh: 袋里装的是三百英镑，全是一便士的硬币。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He insisted on the assistant’s counting the money before he left— 30,000 pennies in all!
rows.zh: 他坚持要店员把钱数清以后自己才走——总共三万枚一便士硬币！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: On another occasion, he invited a number of important critics to see his private collection of modern paintings.
rows.zh: 还有一次，他邀请了许多重要的评论家来参观他私人收藏的现代绘画。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This exhibition received a great deal of attention in the press, for though the pictures were supposed to be the work of famous artists, they had in fact been painted by Dickie.
rows.zh: 这次展览引起了报界的广泛关注；这些画虽然号称出自名家之手，实际上却全是迪基自己画的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It took him four years to stage this elaborate joke simply to prove that critics do not always know what they are talking about.
rows.zh: 为了策划这场煞费苦心的玩笑，他花了四年时间，只是要证明评论家并非总知道自己在说些什么。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.meaning: 引起别人对自己的注意
usage.note: draw attention to 后接被关注的人或事；反身代词要随主语变化。

usage.exampleZh: 真正的怪人从不会刻意设法引人注意。

usage.note: 表示什么也没说，可描述离开或接受某事时的沉默。

usage.exampleZh: 迪基一声不吭地离开商店，又提着一只大布袋回来了。

usage.note: to 是介词，后接人、事或动名词；paid 是 pay 的过去式。

usage.note: 常放在数量后或句末，用来说明总数。
usage.example: He insisted on the assistant’s counting the money before he left— 30,000 pennies in all!

rows.en: The salvage operation had been a complete failure.
rows.zh: 这次打捞行动彻底失败了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The small ship, Elkor, which had been searching the Barents Sea for weeks, was on its way home.
rows.zh: 小船“埃尔科号”在巴伦支海搜寻了几个星期，现在正驶向归途。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A radio message from the mainland had been received by the ship’s captain instructing him to give up the search.
rows.zh: 船长已经收到了大陆发来的一封无线电报，指示他放弃搜寻。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The captain knew that another attempt would be made later, for the sunken ship he was trying to find had been carrying a precious cargo of gold bullion.
rows.zh: 船长知道以后还会再次尝试，因为他一直在寻找的那艘沉船当时载着一批贵重的金条。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Despite the message, the captain of the Elkor decided to try once more.
rows.zh: 尽管收到了电报，“埃尔科号”的船长还是决定再试一次。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The sea bed was scoured with powerful nets and there was tremendous excitement on board when a chest was raised from the bottom.
rows.zh: 船员用结实的大网搜遍海底；当一只箱子从海底被吊上来时，全船都激动不已。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though the crew were at first under the impression that the lost ship had been found, the contents of the chest proved them wrong.
rows.zh: 船员们起初以为找到了要找的沉船，可箱里的东西证明他们弄错了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: What they had in fact found was a ship which had been sunk many years before.
rows.zh: 他们实际找到的是一艘多年前就已沉没的船。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The chest contained the personal belongings of a seaman, Alan Fielding.
rows.zh: 箱里装着海员艾伦·菲尔丁的私人物品。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There were books, clothing and photographs, together with letters which the seaman had once received from his wife.
rows.zh: 里面有书、衣服和照片，还有这位海员生前收到的妻子来信。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The captain of the Elkor ordered his men to salvage as much as possible from the wreck.
rows.zh: “埃尔科号”的船长命令手下尽可能多地从沉船上打捞物品。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Nothing of value was found, but the numerous items which were brought to the surface proved to be of great interest.
rows.zh: 虽然没找到值钱的东西，但打捞上来的众多物件却十分引人关注。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: From a heavy gun that was raised, the captain realized that the ship must have been a cruiser.
rows.zh: 从吊上来的一门重炮判断，船长意识到这艘船一定是巡洋舰。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In another chest, which contained the belongings of a ship’s officer, there was an unfinished letter which had been written on March 14th, 1943.
rows.zh: 另一只箱子里装的是一位舰上军官的物品，其中有一封写于一九四三年三月十四日、尚未写完的信。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The captain learnt from the letter that the name of the lost ship was the Karen.
rows.zh: 船长从信中得知，这艘沉船叫“卡伦号”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The most valuable find of all was the ship’s log book, parts of which it was still possible to read.
rows.zh: 最有价值的发现是船上的航海日志，其中有些部分的字迹仍然可以辨认。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: From this the captain was able to piece together all the information that had come to light.
rows.zh: 船长凭着这本日志，把已经发现的所有信息拼凑了起来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Karen had been sailing in a convoy to Russia when she was torpedoed by an enemy submarine.
rows.zh: “卡伦号”当时随一支护航船队驶往俄罗斯，途中被敌方潜艇的鱼雷击中。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This was later confirmed by a naval official at the Ministry of Defence after the Elkor had returned home.
rows.zh: “埃尔科号”返航后，国防部的一位海军官员随后证实了这一情况。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All the items that were found were sent to the War Museum.
rows.zh: 找到的所有物品都被送进了战争博物馆。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We have all experienced days when everything goes wrong.
rows.zh: 我们都经历过事事不顺的日子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A day may begin well enough, but suddenly everything seems to get out of control.
rows.zh: 一天开始时也许还挺顺利，可突然间，一切似乎都失去了控制。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: What invariably happens is that a great number of things choose to go wrong at precisely the same moment.
rows.zh: 总会出现这样的情形：一大堆事情偏偏在同一时刻出了岔子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is as if a single unimportant event set up a chain of reactions.
rows.zh: 仿佛一件微不足道的小事引发了一连串反应。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Let us suppose that you are preparing a meal and keeping an eye on the baby at the same time.
rows.zh: 假设你一边做饭，一边照看孩子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The telephone rings and this marks the prelude to an unforeseen series of catastrophes.
rows.zh: 电话铃响了，这就拉开了一连串意想不到的灾难的序幕。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: While you are on the phone, the baby pulls the tablecloth off the table, smashing half your best crockery and cutting himself in the process.
rows.zh: 你正打着电话，孩子把桌布从桌上拽下来，摔碎了你一半最好的餐具，还在这过程中划伤了自己。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: You hang up hurriedly and attend to baby, crockery, etc. Meanwhile, the meal gets burnt.
rows.zh: 你匆忙挂断电话，去照料孩子、收拾餐具等等；与此同时，饭菜烧焦了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As if this were not enough to reduce you to tears, your husband arrives, unexpectedly bringing three guests to dinner.
rows.zh: 这些仿佛还不足以让你哭出来似的，你丈夫回来了，还出乎意料地带了三位客人来吃饭。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Things can go wrong on a big scale, as a number of people recently discovered in Parramatta, a suburb of Sydney.
rows.zh: 出乱子也能波及很大范围，悉尼郊区帕拉马塔的一些人最近就发现了这一点。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: During the rush hour one evening two cars collided and both drivers began to argue.
rows.zh: 一天傍晚的交通高峰期，两辆汽车相撞，两位司机争吵了起来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The woman immediately behind the two cars happened to be a learner.
rows.zh: 紧跟在这两辆车后面的女司机碰巧还是个学车的新手。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She suddenly got into a panic and stopped her car.
rows.zh: 她一下慌了神，把车停了下来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This made the driver following her brake hard.
rows.zh: 这使跟在她后面的司机猛踩刹车。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: His wife was sitting beside him holding a large cake.
rows.zh: 他的妻子坐在他身旁，手里捧着一只大蛋糕。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As she was thrown forward, the cake went right through the windscreen and landed on the road.
rows.zh: 她的身体被猛地甩向前方，蛋糕径直穿过挡风玻璃，落到了马路上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Seeing a cake flying through the air, a lorry driver who was drawing up alongside the car, pulled up all of a sudden.
rows.zh: 一位卡车司机正把车开到这辆汽车旁边，看到一个蛋糕在空中飞来，突然停下了车。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The lorry was loaded with empty beer bottles and hundreds of them slid off the back of the vehicle and on to the road.
rows.zh: 卡车上装满了空啤酒瓶，几百只瓶子从车尾滑落到路面上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This led to yet another angry argument.
rows.zh: 这又引发了一场怒气冲冲的争吵。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Meanwhile, the traffic piled up behind.
rows.zh: 与此同时，后面的车辆越堵越多。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It took the police nearly an hour to get the traffic on the move again.
rows.zh: 警察用了将近一小时，才使车辆重新通行。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the meantime, the lorry driver had to sweep up hundreds of broken bottles.
rows.zh: 在此期间，卡车司机不得不清扫几百只摔碎的瓶子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Only two stray dogs benefited from all this confusion, for they greedily devoured what was left of the cake.
rows.zh: 只有两条流浪狗从这场混乱中得了好处，它们贪婪地吞吃了剩下的蛋糕。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was just one of those days!
rows.zh: 这可真是诸事不顺的一天！
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 可指事情出岔子或计划不顺，不一定指做错道德上的事。

usage.exampleZh: 我们都经历过事事不顺的日子。

usage.note: get 强调从可控变为失控的过程。

usage.exampleZh: 一天开始时也许还挺顺利，可突然间，一切似乎都失去了控制。

usage.note: 表示一边做别的事一边留心，eye 在这个短语中用单数。
usage.example: Let us suppose that you are preparing a meal and keeping an eye on the baby at the same time.
usage.exampleZh: 假设你一边做饭，一边照看孩子。

usage.note: 表示进入惊慌状态；panic 作可数名词时可用 a panic。
usage.example: She suddenly got into a panic and stopped her car.
usage.exampleZh: 她一下慌了神，把车停了下来。

usage.note: 固定说法，相当于 suddenly，其中有 a。
usage.example: Seeing a cake flying through the air, a lorry driver who was drawing up alongside the car, pulled up all of a sudden.
usage.exampleZh: 一位卡车司机正把车开到这辆汽车旁边，看到一个蛋糕在空中飞来，突然停下了车。

usage.note: from 引出好处的来源；可用于人、组织或事物。

usage.exampleZh: 只有两条流浪狗从这场混乱中得了好处，它们贪婪地吞吃了剩下的蛋糕。

rows.en: Antique shops exert a peculiar fascination on a great many people.
rows.zh: 古董店对许多人有一种特别的吸引力。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The more expensive kind of antique shop where rare objects are beautifully displayed in glass cases to keep them free from dust is usually a forbidding place.
rows.zh: 价格较高的那类古董店通常令人望而却步，店里把稀罕物件精美地陈列在玻璃柜中，以免沾上灰尘。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But no one has to muster up courage to enter a less pretentious antique shop.
rows.zh: 不过，走进一家不那么讲排场的古董店，谁也用不着鼓起勇气。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There is always hope that in its labyrinth of musty, dark, disordered rooms a real rarity will be found amongst the piles of assorted junk that litter the floors.
rows.zh: 在那些迷宫般霉味扑鼻、昏暗杂乱的房间里，地上堆着各式各样的废旧东西，人们总抱着能从中找到真正珍品的希望。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: No one discovers a rarity by chance.
rows.zh: 谁也不是单凭偶然就能发现珍品的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A truly dedicated bargain hunter must have patience, and above all, the ability to recognize the worth of something when he sees it.
rows.zh: 一个真正热衷于淘便宜货的人必须有耐心，最重要的是，东西一到眼前就能看出它的价值。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: To do this, he must be at least as knowledgeable as the dealer.
rows.zh: 要做到这一点，他至少得和古董商一样内行。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Like a scientist bent on making a discovery, he must cherish the hope that one day he will be amply rewarded.
rows.zh: 就像一位一心要有所发现的科学家，他必须珍视这样的希望：总有一天自己会得到丰厚的回报。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: My old friend, Frank Halliday, is just such a person.
rows.zh: 我的老朋友弗兰克·哈利迪就是这样一个人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He has often described to me how he picked up a masterpiece for a mere £50.
rows.zh: 他常向我讲述自己如何只花五十英镑就淘到了一幅名作。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One Saturday morning, Frank visited an antique shop in my neighbourhood.
rows.zh: 一个星期六的上午，弗兰克走进了我家附近的一家古董店。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As he had never been there before, he found a great deal to interest him.
rows.zh: 他以前从没去过那里，因而发现许多东西都让他感兴趣。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The morning passed rapidly and Frank was about to leave when he noticed a large packing case lying on the floor.
rows.zh: 一上午很快过去了，弗兰克正要离开，忽然看见地上放着一个大包装箱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The dealer told him that it had just come in, but that he could not be bothered to open it.
rows.zh: 店主告诉他，这箱东西刚送来，不过他懒得打开。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Frank begged him to do so and the dealer reluctantly prised it open.
rows.zh: 弗兰克恳求他打开，店主这才不大情愿地把箱子撬开。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The contents were disappointing.
rows.zh: 箱里的东西令人失望。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Apart from an interesting-looking carved dagger, the box was full of crockery, much of it broken.
rows.zh: 除了一把样子颇有趣、带雕饰的短剑以外，箱里全是陶瓷餐具，而且大多已经破损。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Frank gently lifted the crockery out of the box and suddenly noticed a miniature painting at the bottom of the packing case.
rows.zh: 弗兰克把餐具轻轻地从箱中取出，突然发现箱底有一幅微型画。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As its composition and line reminded him of an Italian painting he knew well, he decided to buy it.
rows.zh: 画的构图和线条使他想起一幅自己很熟悉的意大利画作，他于是决定买下它。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Glancing at it briefly, the dealer told him that it was worth £50.
rows.zh: 店主匆匆瞥了一眼，告诉他这画值五十英镑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Frank could hardly conceal his excitement, for he knew that he had made a real discovery.
rows.zh: 弗兰克几乎掩饰不住自己的兴奋，因为他知道自己确实发现了宝贝。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The tiny painting proved to be an unknown masterpiece by Correggio and was worth hundreds of thousands of pounds.
rows.zh: 这幅小画后来被证实是科雷乔一幅此前不为人知的杰作，价值数十万英镑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: muster up 常与 courage、energy 等搭配，强调努力调动起所需的力量。
usage.example: But no one has to muster up courage to enter a less pretentious antique shop.
usage.exampleZh: 不过，走进一家不那么讲排场的古董店，谁也用不着鼓起勇气。

usage.note: 表示事情碰巧发生；也可用于否定句，强调并非偶然。
usage.example: No one discovers a rarity by chance.
usage.exampleZh: 谁也不是单凭偶然就能发现珍品的。

usage.note: 用于突出几项条件中最关键的一项。
usage.example: A truly dedicated bargain hunter must have patience, and above all, the ability to recognize the worth of something when he sees it.
usage.exampleZh: 一个真正热衷于淘便宜货的人必须有耐心，最重要的是，东西一到眼前就能看出它的价值。

usage.note: on 后接名词或动名词，常带意志坚定甚至执意如此的意味。
usage.example: Like a scientist bent on making a discovery, he must cherish the hope that one day he will be amply rewarded.
usage.exampleZh: 就像一位一心要有所发现的科学家，他必须珍视这样的希望：总有一天自己会得到丰厚的回报。

usage.note: 表达不确定的大致数量时 hundreds 和 thousands 都用复数，后面保留 of。
usage.example: The tiny painting proved to be an unknown masterpiece by Correggio and was worth hundreds of thousands of pounds.
usage.exampleZh: 这幅小画后来被证实是科雷乔一幅此前不为人知的杰作，价值数十万英镑。

rows.en: The word justice is usually associated with courts of law.
rows.zh: “正义”这个词通常使人联想到法庭。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We might say that justice has been done when a man’s innocence or guilt has been proved beyond doubt.
rows.zh: 当一个人无罪或有罪已被确凿地证实后，我们也许会说正义得到了伸张。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Justice is part of the complex machinery of the law.
rows.zh: 正义是法律这套复杂运作机制的一部分。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Those who seek it undertake an arduous journey and can never be sure that they will find it.
rows.zh: 寻求正义的人踏上的是一段艰辛的旅程，而且永远无法确定自己最终能否找到它。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Judges, however wise or eminent, are human and can make mistakes.
rows.zh: 法官无论多么睿智、多么显赫，也都是人，照样可能犯错。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There are rare instances when justice almost ceases to be an abstract concept.
rows.zh: 极少数时候，正义几乎不再只是一个抽象的概念。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Reward or punishment are meted out quite independent of human interference.
rows.zh: 奖赏或惩罚的降临，完全不受人为干预。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At such times, justice acts like a living force.
rows.zh: 在这种时候，正义仿佛是一股有生命的力量。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When we use a phrase like ‘it serves him right’, we are, in part, admitting that a certain set of circumstances has enabled justice to act of its own accord.
rows.zh: 当我们说“他活该”这样的话时，也就在某种程度上承认，某些特定的情形使正义得以自行发挥作用。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When a thief was caught on the premises of a large jewellery store one morning, the shop assistants must have found it impossible to resist the temptation to say ‘it serves him right’.
rows.zh: 一天上午，一个小偷在一家大珠宝店里被抓住，店员们一定忍不住想说“他活该”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The shop was an old converted house with many large, disused fireplaces and tall, narrow chimneys.
rows.zh: 这家商店由一栋老房子改建而成，里面有许多废弃的大壁炉和又高又窄的烟囱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Towards midday, a girl heard a muffled cry coming from behind one of the walls.
rows.zh: 快到中午时，一位女店员听到一面墙后传来低沉的呼救声。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As the cry was repeated several times, she ran to tell the manager who promptly rang up the fire brigade.
rows.zh: 呼救声接连响了几次，她就跑去告诉经理，经理立即打电话叫来了消防队。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The cry had certainly come from one of the chimneys, but as there were so many of them, the fire fighters could not be certain which one it was.
rows.zh: 声音肯定来自某根烟囱，但烟囱太多，消防员一时无法确定是哪一根。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They located the right chimney by tapping at the walls and listening for the man’s cries.
rows.zh: 他们一边敲墙，一边听那人的呼喊，终于找对了烟囱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After chipping through a wall which was eighteen inches thick, they found that a man had been trapped in the chimney.
rows.zh: 凿穿一堵十八英寸厚的墙以后，他们发现有个人困在烟囱里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As it was extremely narrow, the man was unable to move, but the fire fighters were eventually able to free him by cutting a huge hole in the wall.
rows.zh: 烟囱极窄，那人动弹不得；不过，消防员最后在墙上凿出一个大洞，把他解救了出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The sorry-looking, blackened figure that emerged, admitted at once that he had tried to break into the shop during the night but had got stuck in the chimney.
rows.zh: 这个出来时满身漆黑、模样狼狈的人立刻承认，他夜里曾试图闯进商店，却卡在了烟囱里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He had been there for nearly ten hours.
rows.zh: 他已经在那里待了将近十个小时。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Justice had been done even before the man was handed over to the police.
rows.zh: 那人还没被移交给警察，正义就已经得到了伸张。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 常用被动形式表达概念上的联系；with 后接联想到的事物。
usage.example: The word justice is usually associated with courts of law.
usage.exampleZh: “正义”这个词通常使人联想到法庭。

usage.note: 用于强调证据或结论没有合理疑问，常接在 prove 之后。

usage.exampleZh: 当一个人无罪或有罪已被确凿地证实后，我们也许会说正义得到了伸张。

usage.note: 表示没有外力推动便自行发生；one’s 随主语变化。
usage.example: When we use a phrase like ‘it serves him right’, we are, in part, admitting that a certain set of circumstances has enabled justice to act of its own accord.
usage.exampleZh: 当我们说“他活该”这样的话时，也就在某种程度上承认，某些特定的情形使正义得以自行发挥作用。

usage.note: 这里指非法进入建筑物，不要与表示进入某行业的引申义混淆。
usage.example: The sorry-looking, blackened figure that emerged, admitted at once that he had tried to break into the shop during the night but had got stuck in the chimney.
usage.exampleZh: 这个出来时满身漆黑、模样狼狈的人立刻承认，他夜里曾试图闯进商店，却卡在了烟囱里。

usage.note: 可说 hand someone over to the police；代词作宾语时放在 hand 与 over 之间。
usage.example: Justice had been done even before the man was handed over to the police.
usage.exampleZh: 那人还没被移交给警察，正义就已经得到了伸张。

rows.en: We are less credulous than we used to be.
rows.zh: 我们如今不像过去那样轻信了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the nineteenth century, a novelist would bring his story to a conclusion by presenting his readers with a series of coincidences — most of them wildly improbable.
rows.zh: 十九世纪的小说家常用一连串巧合来收束故事，其中大多数巧合都离奇得令人难以相信。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Readers happily accepted the fact that an obscure maidservant was really the hero’s mother.
rows.zh: 一个不起眼的女仆竟然是男主人公的母亲，读者也欣然接受。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A long-lost brother, who was presumed dead, was really alive all the time and wickedly plotting to bring about the hero’s downfall.
rows.zh: 一个失散多年、被认为已经死去的兄弟，其实一直活着，还在恶毒地密谋让男主人公垮台。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And so on.
rows.zh: 诸如此类。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Modern readers would find such naive solutions totally unacceptable.
rows.zh: 现代读者会觉得，这样天真的结局安排完全无法接受。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Yet, in real life, circumstances do sometimes conspire to bring about coincidences which anyone but a nineteenth century novelist would find incredible.
rows.zh: 然而在现实生活中，各种情形有时确实会凑在一起，造成一些巧合，除了十九世纪的小说家，任何人都会觉得不可思议。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When I was a boy, my grandfather told me how a German taxi driver, Franz Bussman, found a brother who was thought to have been killed twenty years before.
rows.zh: 我小时候，祖父曾告诉我，一个名叫弗朗茨·巴斯曼的德国出租车司机，如何找到了被认为二十年前就已遇难的兄弟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: While on a walking tour with his wife, he stopped to talk to a workman.
rows.zh: 他和妻子在徒步旅行途中停下来，同一个工人聊了几句。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After they had gone on, Mrs. Bussman commented on the workman's close resemblance to her husband and even suggested that he might be his brother.
rows.zh: 他们继续往前走后，巴斯曼夫人谈到那工人的相貌和丈夫极其相像，甚至提出那人也许就是他的兄弟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Franz poured scorn on the idea, pointing out that his brother had been killed in action during the war.
rows.zh: 弗朗茨对这个想法嗤之以鼻，并指出自己的兄弟在战争中已经阵亡。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though Mrs. Bussman was fully acquainted with this story, she thought that there was a chance in a million that she might be right.
rows.zh: 巴斯曼夫人虽然对这件往事一清二楚，却觉得自己的猜测也许还有百万分之一的可能是对的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A few days later, she sent a boy to the workman to ask him if his name was Hans Bussman.
rows.zh: 几天后，她派一个男孩去找那个工人，问他是否叫汉斯·巴斯曼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Needless to say, the man’s name was Hans Bussman and he really was Franz’s long-lost brother.
rows.zh: 不用说，那人果然叫汉斯·巴斯曼，而且确实就是弗朗茨失散多年的兄弟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When the brothers were reunited, Hans explained how it was that he was still alive.
rows.zh: 兄弟俩重逢时，汉斯解释了自己究竟是怎样活下来的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After having been wounded towards the end of the war, he had been sent to hospital and was separated from his unit.
rows.zh: 战争将近结束时，他负了伤，被送进医院，因此和部队失去了联系。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The hospital had been bombed and Hans had made his way back into Western Germany on foot.
rows.zh: 医院遭到轰炸，汉斯步行返回了德国西部。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Meanwhile, his unit was lost and all records of him had been destroyed.
rows.zh: 这期间，他所在的部队已不复存在，关于他的全部档案也都毁掉了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Hans returned to his family home, but the house had been bombed and no one in the neighbourhood knew what had become of the inhabitants.
rows.zh: 汉斯回到了家，可房子已经被炸毁，邻居们谁也不知道原来的住户后来怎么样了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Assuming that his family had been killed during an air raid, Hans settled down in a village fifty miles away where he had remained ever since.
rows.zh: 汉斯以为家人都死于一次空袭，就在五十英里外的一个村子定居下来，从此一直住在那里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.exampleZh: 十九世纪的小说家常用一连串巧合来收束故事，其中大多数巧合都离奇得令人难以相信。

usage.note: 常搭配 change、downfall 等结果，不表示把具体物品带来。
usage.example: A long-lost brother, who was presumed dead, was really alive all the time and wickedly plotting to bring about the hero’s downfall.
usage.exampleZh: 一个失散多年、被认为已经死去的兄弟，其实一直活着，还在恶毒地密谋让男主人公垮台。

usage.note: scorn 表示强烈轻蔑，语气比普通的 disagree 更重。
usage.example: Franz poured scorn on the idea, pointing out that his brother had been killed in action during the war.
usage.exampleZh: 弗朗茨对这个想法嗤之以鼻，并指出自己的兄弟在战争中已经阵亡。

usage.note: 常作句首评注语，引出读者可以预料到的情况。
usage.example: Needless to say, the man’s name was Hans Bussman and he really was Franz’s long-lost brother.
usage.exampleZh: 不用说，那人果然叫汉斯·巴斯曼，而且确实就是弗朗茨失散多年的兄弟。

rows.en: We have learnt to expect that trains will be punctual.
rows.zh: 我们已经习惯了认为火车应当准时。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After years of conditioning, most of us have developed an unshakable faith in railway timetables.
rows.zh: 经过多年的习惯养成，我们大多数人对铁路时刻表有了不可动摇的信任。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Ships may be delayed by storms; flights may be cancelled because of bad weather; but trains must be on time.
rows.zh: 轮船可能因风暴而延误，航班可能因恶劣天气而取消，但火车一定得准点。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Only an exceptionally heavy snowfall might temporarily dislocate railway services.
rows.zh: 只有格外猛烈的降雪，才可能暂时打乱铁路运输。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is all too easy to blame the railway authorities when something does go wrong.
rows.zh: 一旦真出了什么岔子，人们太容易把责任推给铁路部门了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The truth is that when mistakes occur, they are more likely to be ours than theirs.
rows.zh: 事实上，出了差错时，更有可能是我们自己出了错，而非铁路部门。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After consulting my railway timetable, I noted with satisfaction that there was an express train to Westhaven.
rows.zh: 查过铁路时刻表以后，我满意地发现有一班开往韦斯特黑文的快车。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It went direct from my local station and the journey lasted a mere hour and seventeen minutes.
rows.zh: 它从我当地的车站直达目的地，全程只需一小时十七分钟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When I boarded the train, I could not help noticing that a great many local people got on as well.
rows.zh: 上车时，我不由得注意到还有很多当地人也上了车。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At the time, this did not strike me as odd.
rows.zh: 当时我并不觉得这有什么奇怪。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I reflected that there must be a great many people besides myself who wished to take advantage of this excellent service.
rows.zh: 我想，除我以外，一定还有许多人也希望享受这么好的列车服务。
rows.speaker: 叙述者

rows.en: Neither was I surprised when the train stopped at Widley, a tiny station a few miles along the line.
rows.zh: 列车在沿线几英里外的一个小站威德利停下时，我也并不惊讶。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even a mighty express train can be held up by signals.
rows.zh: 就连气势十足的快车，也可能因为信号而停下来等候。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But when the train dawdled at station after station, I began to wonder.
rows.zh: 可是，火车一站接着一站地磨蹭，我便开始犯嘀咕了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It suddenly dawned on me that this express was not roaring down the line at ninety miles an hour, but barely chugging along at thirty.
rows.zh: 我猛然明白，这趟快车并没有以每小时九十英里的速度沿着铁路线疾驰，而是在以勉强每小时三十英里的速度吭哧吭哧地慢行。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One hour and seventeen minutes passed and we had not even covered half the distance.
rows.zh: 一小时十七分钟过去了，我们连一半的路程都还没走完。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I asked a passenger if this was the Westhaven Express, but he had not even heard of it.
rows.zh: 我问一位乘客这是不是韦斯特黑文快车，他却连听都没听说过。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I determined to lodge a complaint as soon as we arrived.
rows.zh: 我打定主意，一到站就提出投诉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Two hours later, I was talking angrily to the station master at Westhaven.
rows.zh: 两小时后，我正在韦斯特黑文气愤地向站长诉说。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When he denied the train’s existence, I borrowed his copy of the timetable.
rows.zh: 站长说根本没有这趟列车，我就借来了他的时刻表。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There was a note of triumph in my voice when I told him that it was there in black and white.
rows.zh: 我告诉他表上白纸黑字写着呢，声音里带着几分得意。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Glancing at it briefly, he told me to look again.
rows.zh: 他匆匆瞥了一眼，叫我再仔细看看。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A tiny asterisk conducted me to a footnote at the bottom of the page.
rows.zh: 一个小小的星号把我的视线引到了页面底部的一条注释上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It said: ‘This service has been suspended.’
rows.zh: 上面写着：“本次列车已停运。”
rows.speaker: 铁路时刻表注释

usage.example: Ships may be delayed by storms; flights may be cancelled because of bad weather; but trains must be on time.
usage.exampleZh: 轮船可能因风暴而延误，航班可能因恶劣天气而取消，但火车一定得准点。

usage.note: does go wrong 中 does 用来加强语气，go 仍用原形。
usage.example: It is all too easy to blame the railway authorities when something does go wrong.
usage.exampleZh: 一旦真出了什么岔子，人们太容易把责任推给铁路部门了。

usage.note: cannot help 后接动名词，表示无法抑制某种反应；不是不能帮助。
usage.example: When I boarded the train, I could not help noticing that a great many local people got on as well.
usage.exampleZh: 上车时，我不由得注意到还有很多当地人也上了车。

usage.note: 常用 it dawns on someone that... 表示某个道理逐渐或突然进入意识。
usage.example: It suddenly dawned on me that this express was not roaring down the line at ninety miles an hour, but barely chugging along at thirty.
usage.exampleZh: 我猛然明白，这趟快车并没有以每小时九十英里的速度沿着铁路线疾驰，而是在以勉强每小时三十英里的速度吭哧吭哧地慢行。

usage.note: 这里指书面记载清清楚楚，可用来强调有文字为证。
usage.example: There was a note of triumph in my voice when I told him that it was there in black and white.
usage.exampleZh: 我告诉他表上白纸黑字写着呢，声音里带着几分得意。

rows.en: Future historians will be in a unique position when they come to record the history of our own times.
rows.zh: 未来的历史学家在记述我们这个时代的历史时，将具备独特的有利条件。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They will hardly know which facts to select from the great mass of evidence that steadily accumulates.
rows.zh: 面对不断积累的大量史料，他们几乎不知道该挑选哪些事实才好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: What is more, they will not have to rely solely on the written word.
rows.zh: 而且，他们不必只依赖文字记载。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Films, videos, CDs and CD-ROMs are just some of the bewildering amount of information they will have.
rows.zh: 电影、录像、光盘和只读光盘，不过是他们届时掌握的、数量多得令人眼花缭乱的信息中的一部分。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They will be able, as it were, to see and hear us in action.
rows.zh: 可以说，他们将能亲眼看见、亲耳听见我们活动时的情形。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But the historian attempting to reconstruct the distant past is always faced with a difficult task.
rows.zh: 然而，想要重建遥远往昔的历史学家，总会面临一项艰难的任务。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He has to deduce what he can from the few scanty clues available.
rows.zh: 他只能根据现存的寥寥几条线索，尽可能作出推断。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even seemingly insignificant remains can shed interesting light on the history of early man.
rows.zh: 即使看似无关紧要的遗存，也能为理解早期人类的历史提供有意思的启示。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Up to now, historians have assumed that calendars came into being with the advent of agriculture, for then man was faced with a real need to understand something about the seasons.
rows.zh: 迄今为止，历史学家一直认为，历法随着农业的出现而产生，因为到了那时，人类才真正需要对季节有所了解。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Recent scientific evidence seems to indicate that this assumption is incorrect.
rows.zh: 近来的科学证据似乎表明，这个假设并不正确。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Historians have long been puzzled by dots, lines and symbols which have been engraved on walls, bones, and the ivory tusks of mammoths.
rows.zh: 刻在墙壁、骨头和猛犸象牙上的那些点、线和符号，长期以来一直困扰着历史学家。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The nomads who made these markings lived by hunting and fishing during the last Ice Age which began about 35,000 B.C. and ended about 10,000 B.C.
rows.zh: 留下这些记号的游牧人，生活在大约始于公元前三万五千年、终于公元前一万年的最后一个冰期，以狩猎和捕鱼为生。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: By correlating markings made in various parts of the world, historians have been able to read this difficult code.
rows.zh: 通过比对世界各地的记号，历史学家已经能够解读这种难懂的密码。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They have found that it is connected with the passage of days and the phases of the moon.
rows.zh: 他们发现，它与日子的流逝和月相的变化有关。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is, in fact, a primitive type of calendar.
rows.zh: 实际上，这是一种原始的历法。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It has long been known that the hunting scenes depicted on walls were not simply a form of artistic expression.
rows.zh: 人们早已知道，墙壁上描绘的狩猎场景并非仅仅是艺术表现形式。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They had a definite meaning, for they were as near as early man could get to writing.
rows.zh: 这些画面具有明确的含义，因为对早期人类而言，它们已是最接近文字的表达方式。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is possible that there is a definite relation between these paintings and the markings that sometimes accompany them.
rows.zh: 这些画与有时出现在它们旁边的记号之间，可能存在某种确定的联系。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It seems that man was making a real effort to understand the seasons 20,000 years earlier than has been supposed.
rows.zh: 看来，人类开始认真尝试了解季节的时间，比过去推测的还早两万年。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 在已有论据之外补充一层意思，常在句首后接逗号。
usage.example: What is more, they will not have to rely solely on the written word.
usage.exampleZh: 而且，他们不必只依赖文字记载。

usage.note: 用于提示后面的说法带有比喻或不完全按字面理解的意味。
usage.example: They will be able, as it were, to see and hear us in action.
usage.exampleZh: 可以说，他们将能亲眼看见、亲耳听见我们活动时的情形。

usage.note: shed light on 表示帮助澄清问题，light 在这里是不可数名词。
usage.example: Even seemingly insignificant remains can shed interesting light on the history of early man.
usage.exampleZh: 即使看似无关紧要的遗存，也能为理解早期人类的历史提供有意思的启示。

usage.note: 表示事物出现，不等于表示实行的 come into effect。
usage.example: Up to now, historians have assumed that calendars came into being with the advent of agriculture, for then man was faced with a real need to understand something about the seasons.
usage.exampleZh: 迄今为止，历史学家一直认为，历法随着农业的出现而产生，因为到了那时，人类才真正需要对季节有所了解。

usage.note: 描述事物之间的联系；with 后接相关对象。
usage.example: They have found that it is connected with the passage of days and the phases of the moon.
usage.exampleZh: 他们发现，它与日子的流逝和月相的变化有关。

rows.en: The rough road across the plain soon became so bad that we tried to get Bruce to drive back to the village we had come from.
rows.zh: 穿过平原的那条崎岖道路很快就糟糕得让我们试图劝布鲁斯把车开回出发的村庄。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even though the road was littered with boulders and pitted with holes, Bruce was not in the least perturbed.
rows.zh: 尽管路上大石遍地、坑洼密布，布鲁斯却丝毫不为所动。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Glancing at his map, he informed us that the next village was a mere twenty miles away.
rows.zh: 他瞥了一眼地图，告诉我们下一个村子离这里只有二十英里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was not that Bruce always underestimated difficulties.
rows.zh: 这并不是说布鲁斯总把困难估计得太轻。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He simply had no sense of danger at all.
rows.zh: 他只是完全没有危险意识。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: No matter what the conditions were, he believed that a car should be driven as fast as it could possibly go.
rows.zh: 无论路况怎样，他都认为车就应该开到能开的最快速度。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As we bumped over the dusty track, we swerved to avoid large boulders.
rows.zh: 我们在尘土飞扬的小路上颠簸前进，不时急转方向躲避大石。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The wheels scooped up stones which hammered ominously under the car.
rows.zh: 车轮卷起石块，石块在车底敲得砰砰响，让人觉得不祥。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We felt sure that sooner or later a stone would rip a hole in our petrol tank or damage the engine.
rows.zh: 我们认定，迟早会有石块把油箱划出一个洞，或者把发动机撞坏。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Because of this, we kept looking back, wondering if we were leaving a trail of oil and petrol behind us.
rows.zh: 正因为如此，我们不断向后张望，担心身后是不是已经留下一路机油和汽油。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: What a relief it was when the boulders suddenly disappeared, giving way to a stretch of plain where the only obstacles were clumps of bushes.
rows.zh: 大石突然不见了，眼前换成一片平地，障碍只剩下一丛丛灌木，我们不禁大大松了口气。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But there was worse to come.
rows.zh: 可是，更糟的事还在后头。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Just ahead of us there was a huge fissure.
rows.zh: 就在前面，地上出现了一道大裂缝。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In response to renewed pleadings, Bruce stopped.
rows.zh: 在我们又一次苦苦请求之下，布鲁斯停了车。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though we all got out to examine the fissure, he remained in the car.
rows.zh: 我们都下车查看裂缝，他却仍坐在车里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We informed him that the fissure extended for fifty yards and was two feet wide and four feet deep.
rows.zh: 我们告诉他，这道裂缝长达五十码，宽两英尺，深四英尺。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even this had no effect.
rows.zh: 就连这样也没起作用。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Bruce went into a low gear and drove at a terrifying speed, keeping the front wheels astride the crack as he followed its zigzag course.
rows.zh: 布鲁斯挂上低挡，以吓人的速度往前开，让两个前轮跨在裂缝两侧，沿着弯弯曲曲的裂缝前进。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Before we had time to worry about what might happen, we were back on the plain again.
rows.zh: 我们还来不及担心会出什么事，就又回到了平地上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Bruce consulted the map once more and told us that the village was now only fifteen miles away.
rows.zh: 布鲁斯又看了一次地图，告诉我们现在离村子只有十五英里了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Our next obstacle was a shallow pool of water about half a mile across.
rows.zh: 下一个障碍是一片浅水洼，横跨约半英里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Bruce charged at it, but in the middle, the car came to a grinding halt.
rows.zh: 布鲁斯驾车冲了进去，可到了中间，车便嘎然停住了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A yellow light on the dashboard flashed angrily and Bruce cheerfully announced that there was no oil in the engine!
rows.zh: 仪表盘上的一盏黄灯气急败坏似的闪着，布鲁斯却兴高采烈地宣布，发动机里没机油了！
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 用来加强否定，常修饰 worried、surprised 等形容词。
usage.example: Even though the road was littered with boulders and pitted with holes, Bruce was not in the least perturbed.
usage.exampleZh: 尽管路上大石遍地、坑洼密布，布鲁斯却丝毫不为所动。

usage.note: 表示时间不确定，但说话人认为事情终会发生。
usage.example: We felt sure that sooner or later a stone would rip a hole in our petrol tank or damage the engine.
usage.exampleZh: 我们认定，迟早会有石块把油箱划出一个洞，或者把发动机撞坏。

usage.note: 这里描述景物转变，不是向某人让步的含义。
usage.example: What a relief it was when the boulders suddenly disappeared, giving way to a stretch of plain where the only obstacles were clumps of bushes.
usage.exampleZh: 大石突然不见了，眼前换成一片平地，障碍只剩下一丛丛灌木，我们不禁大大松了口气。

usage.note: to 是介词，后接请求、变化或刺激等名词。
usage.example: In response to renewed pleadings, Bruce stopped.
usage.exampleZh: 在我们又一次苦苦请求之下，布鲁斯停了车。

usage.meaning: 嘎然停住；突然彻底停下
usage.note: 可形容车辆骤停，也可引申为工作或活动突然停顿。
usage.example: Bruce charged at it, but in the middle, the car came to a grinding halt.
usage.exampleZh: 布鲁斯驾车冲了进去，可到了中间，车便嘎然停住了。

rows.en: It has never been explained why university students seem to enjoy practical jokes more than anyone else.
rows.zh: 大学生为什么似乎比其他人都更喜欢恶作剧，这一点始终没有人解释清楚。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Students specialize in a particular type of practical joke: the hoax.
rows.zh: 学生尤其擅长一种特殊的恶作剧：设骗局捉弄人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Inviting the fire brigade to put out a nonexistent fire is a crude form of deception which no self-respecting student would ever indulge in.
rows.zh: 叫消防队来扑灭根本不存在的火，是一种粗劣的骗术；凡是有自尊心的学生，都不会干这种事。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Students often create amusing situations which are funny to everyone except the victims.
rows.zh: 学生常常制造出一些有趣的场面，除了受害者，人人都觉得好笑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When a student recently saw two workmen using a pneumatic drill outside his university, he immediately telephoned the police and informed them that two students dressed up as workmen were tearing up the road with a pneumatic drill.
rows.zh: 最近，一名学生看见两个工人在大学外用风钻干活，就立刻给警察打电话，说有两个学生装扮成工人，正在用风钻挖马路。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As soon as he had hung up, he went over to the workmen and told them that if a policeman ordered them to go away, they were not to take him seriously.
rows.zh: 电话一挂，他就走到工人跟前，告诉他们，如果有警察叫他们离开，不必当真。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He added that a student had dressed up as a policeman and was playing all sorts of silly jokes on people.
rows.zh: 他还说，有个学生扮成警察，正在到处跟人开各种无聊的玩笑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Both the police and the workmen were grateful to the student for this piece of advance information.
rows.zh: 警察和工人都很感激这个学生提前通风报信。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The student hid in an archway nearby where he could watch and hear everything that went on.
rows.zh: 学生藏进附近一个拱门里，在那里既能看见，又能听见事情的全部经过。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Sure enough, a policeman arrived on the scene and politely asked the workmen to go away.
rows.zh: 果然，一个警察来到了现场，客气地请工人离开。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When he received a very rude reply from one of the workmen, he threatened to remove them by force.
rows.zh: 一个工人非常粗鲁地回了他一句，他便威胁说要动用武力把他们赶走。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The workmen told him to do as he pleased and the policeman telephoned for help.
rows.zh: 工人叫他随便怎么办，警察于是打电话求援。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Shortly afterwards, four more policemen arrived and remonstrated with the workmen.
rows.zh: 没过多久，又来了四个警察，劝告并责备这两个工人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As the men refused to stop working, the police attempted to seize the pneumatic drill.
rows.zh: 工人不肯停工，警察就试图夺走风钻。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The workmen struggled fiercely and one of them lost his temper.
rows.zh: 工人激烈反抗，其中一个发了脾气。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He threatened to call the police.
rows.zh: 他扬言要报警。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At this, the police pointed out ironically that this would hardly be necessary as the men were already under arrest.
rows.zh: 听到这话，警察讥讽地指出，大概没这个必要了，因为他们已经被逮捕了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Pretending to speak seriously, one of the workmen asked if he might make a telephone call before being taken to the station.
rows.zh: 一个工人装出一本正经的样子，问能不能在被带到警察局之前打个电话。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Permission was granted and a policeman accompanied him to a pay phone.
rows.zh: 警察同意了，一个警察陪他走到一部公用电话旁。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Only when he saw that the man was actually telephoning the police did he realize that they had all been the victims of a hoax.
rows.zh: 直到看见那人真的在给警察打电话，这个警察才明白，他们全都成了一场骗局的受害者。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 指用行动捉弄别人，不是单纯讲一个笑话；可用 play a practical joke on someone。
usage.example: It has never been explained why university students seem to enjoy practical jokes more than anyone else.
usage.exampleZh: 大学生为什么似乎比其他人都更喜欢恶作剧，这一点始终没有人解释清楚。

usage.note: as 后接扮演的身份，dress up 也可单独表示盛装或乔装。
usage.example: When a student recently saw two workmen using a pneumatic drill outside his university, he immediately telephoned the police and informed them that two students dressed up as workmen were tearing up the road with a pneumatic drill.
usage.exampleZh: 最近，一名学生看见两个工人在大学外用风钻干活，就立刻给警察打电话，说有两个学生装扮成工人，正在用风钻挖马路。

usage.note: seriously 放在宾语后；也可用 take something seriously 表示认真对待某事。
usage.example: As soon as he had hung up, he went over to the workmen and told them that if a policeman ordered them to go away, they were not to take him seriously.
usage.exampleZh: 电话一挂，他就走到工人跟前，告诉他们，如果有警察叫他们离开，不必当真。

usage.note: 常引出证实预想的结果。
usage.example: Sure enough, a policeman arrived on the scene and politely asked the workmen to go away.
usage.exampleZh: 果然，一个警察来到了现场，客气地请工人离开。

usage.note: temper 在这里指脾气；所有格随发怒的人变化。
usage.example: The workmen struggled fiercely and one of them lost his temper.
usage.exampleZh: 工人激烈反抗，其中一个发了脾气。

usage.note: arrest 在此固定表达中不加冠词，常与 be 或 place 搭配。
usage.example: At this, the police pointed out ironically that this would hardly be necessary as the men were already under arrest.
usage.exampleZh: 听到这话，警察讥讽地指出，大概没这个必要了，因为他们已经被逮捕了。

rows.en: The quiet life of the country has never appealed to me.
rows.zh: 乡村宁静的生活从来没有吸引过我。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: City born and city bred, I have always regarded the country as something you look at through a train window, or something you occasionally visit during the weekend.
rows.zh: 我生在城里、长在城里，一向觉得乡村是坐火车时从车窗里看看的景色，或者偶尔周末去一趟的地方。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Most of my friends live in the city, yet they always go into raptures at the mere mention of the country.
rows.zh: 我的朋友大多住在城里，可是一提到乡村，他们就总会兴奋得赞不绝口。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though they extol the virtues of the peaceful life, only one of them has ever gone to live in the country and he was back in town within six months.
rows.zh: 他们虽然极力赞美宁静生活的种种好处，却只有一个人真的搬到乡下住过，而他不到六个月就回城了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even he still lives under the illusion that country life is somehow superior to town life.
rows.zh: 即便是他，也仍然抱着一种错觉，觉得乡村生活总归比城市生活更好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He is forever talking about the friendly people, the clean atmosphere, the closeness to nature and the gentle pace of living.
rows.zh: 他没完没了地谈论友善的居民、清新的空气、与大自然的亲近，以及悠缓的生活节奏。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Nothing can be compared, he maintains, with the first cockcrow, the twittering of birds at dawn, the sight of the rising sun glinting on the trees and pastures.
rows.zh: 他坚称，无论什么都比不上清晨第一声鸡啼、黎明时鸟儿的啁啾，以及初升的阳光在树木和牧场上闪耀的景象。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This idyllic pastoral scene is only part of the picture.
rows.zh: 这番诗情画意的田园景色，只反映了实际情况的一部分。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: My friend fails to mention the long and friendless winter evenings in front of the TV — virtually the only form of entertainment.
rows.zh: 我的朋友没有提到，冬夜漫长又孤寂，只能守着电视机度日——这实际上是唯一的娱乐。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He says nothing about the poor selection of goods in the shops, or about those unfortunate people who have to travel from the country to the city every day to get to work.
rows.zh: 他也绝口不提商店里可供挑选的商品少得可怜，更不提那些不幸的人，他们每天不得不从乡下赶到城里上班。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Why people are prepared to tolerate a four-hour journey each day for the dubious privilege of living in the country is beyond me.
rows.zh: 为了享受住在乡下这种好处难说的“特权”，人们竟甘愿每天忍受四小时的路程，这真让我无法理解。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They could be saved so much misery and expense if they chose to live in the city where they rightly belong.
rows.zh: 如果他们选择住在本来就适合自己的城里，就能省掉那么多苦恼和开销。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If you can do without the few pastoral pleasures of the country, you will find the city can provide you with the best that life can offer.
rows.zh: 如果你可以舍弃乡村那几样田园乐趣，就会发现，城市能把生活中最美好的享受提供给你。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: You never have to travel miles to see your friends.
rows.zh: 你永远用不着跑上好几英里去看朋友。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They invariably live nearby and are always available for an informal chat or an evening’s entertainment.
rows.zh: 他们总住在附近，随时都能一起随意聊聊天，或者共度一个娱乐之夜。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Some of my acquaintances in the country come up to town once or twice a year to visit the theatre as a special treat.
rows.zh: 我在乡下认识的一些人，每年只进城一两次看戏，把这当作特别的享受。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For them this is a major operation which involves considerable planning.
rows.zh: 对他们来说，这是一件大事，需要做相当多的安排。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As the play draws to its close, they wonder whether they will ever catch that last train home.
rows.zh: 戏快演完时，他们就开始担心，自己到底能不能赶上回家的末班火车。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The city dweller never experiences anxieties of this sort.
rows.zh: 城里人从来不会为这类事情焦虑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The latest exhibitions, films, or plays are only a short bus ride away.
rows.zh: 坐一小段公交车，就能看到最新的展览、电影或戏剧。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Shopping, too, is always a pleasure.
rows.zh: 购物也总是件乐事。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There is so much variety that you never have to make do with second best.
rows.zh: 商品品种如此丰富，你永远不必退而求其次。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Country people run wild when they go shopping in the city and stagger home loaded with as many of the exotic items as they can carry.
rows.zh: 乡下人进城购物时就像脱了缰一般，尽量买满自己能拿得动的新奇物件，满载着踉跄回家。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Nor is the city without its moments of beauty.
rows.zh: 城市也并非没有美丽的时刻。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There is something comforting about the warm glow shed by advertisements on cold wet winter nights.
rows.zh: 在寒冷潮湿的冬夜，广告灯散发出的暖光让人觉得有几分慰藉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Few things could be more impressive than the peace that descends on deserted city streets at weekends when the thousands that travel to work every day are tucked away in their homes in the country.
rows.zh: 每天进城上班的成千上万人，周末都躲回乡下家中，空荡荡的城市街道于是笼罩在一片宁静里；很少有什么景象能比这更让人印象深刻。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It has always been a mystery to me why city dwellers, who appreciate all these things, obstinately pretend that they would prefer to live in the country.
rows.zh: 城里人明明懂得欣赏这一切，却偏要固执地装作更愿意住在乡下，这一直让我百思不解。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 以事物作主语、以人作 to 的宾语；这里不是呼吁的意思。
usage.example: The quiet life of the country has never appealed to me.
usage.exampleZh: 乡村宁静的生活从来没有吸引过我。

usage.note: raptures 用复数，常用 over 或 about 引出令人兴奋的事。
usage.example: Most of my friends live in the city, yet they always go into raptures at the mere mention of the country.
usage.exampleZh: 我的朋友大多住在城里，可是一提到乡村，他们就总会兴奋得赞不绝口。

usage.note: that 引出错觉的具体内容；语气表示说话人认为这想法不符合实际。
usage.example: Even he still lives under the illusion that country life is somehow superior to town life.
usage.exampleZh: 即便是他，也仍然抱着一种错觉，觉得乡村生活总归比城市生活更好。

usage.note: 后接名词或动名词，强调在缺少某物时仍能应付。
usage.example: If you can do without the few pastoral pleasures of the country, you will find the city can provide you with the best that life can offer.
usage.exampleZh: 如果你可以舍弃乡村那几样田园乐趣，就会发现，城市能把生活中最美好的享受提供给你。

usage.note: 主语通常是会议、演出或一段时期；its close 是带所有格的变体。
usage.example: As the play draws to its close, they wonder whether they will ever catch that last train home.
usage.exampleZh: 戏快演完时，他们就开始担心，自己到底能不能赶上回家的末班火车。

usage.note: with 引出并不完全令人满意的替代物，常带退而求其次的意味。
usage.example: There is so much variety that you never have to make do with second best.
usage.exampleZh: 商品品种如此丰富，你永远不必退而求其次。

rows.en: Cave exploration, or pot-holing, as it has come to be known, is a relatively new sport.
rows.zh: 洞穴探险，也就是如今人们所说的“探洞”，是一项相对新兴的运动。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Perhaps it is the desire for solitude or the chance of making an unexpected discovery that lures people down to the depths of the earth.
rows.zh: 也许是渴望独处，也许是期待意外发现的机会，吸引着人们深入地下。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is impossible to give a satisfactory explanation for a pot-holer’s motives.
rows.zh: 要为探洞者的动机作出令人满意的解释，是不可能的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For him, caves have the same peculiar fascination which high mountains have for the climber.
rows.zh: 对探洞者来说，洞穴有着一种特殊的吸引力，正如高山之于登山者一样。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They arouse instincts which can only be dimly understood.
rows.zh: 它们唤起了某些本能，而人们对这些本能只能模糊地理解。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Exploring really deep caves is not a task for the Sunday afternoon rambler.
rows.zh: 探察真正深邃的洞穴，可不是周日下午悠闲散步的人所能胜任的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Such undertakings require the precise planning and foresight of military operations.
rows.zh: 这种行动需要像军事行动一样周密地筹划，预先考虑各种情况。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It can take as long as eight days to rig up rope ladders and to establish supply bases before a descent can be made into a very deep cave.
rows.zh: 在能够下到一个极深的洞穴之前，光是架设绳梯、建立补给基地，就可能需要长达八天。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Precautions of this sort are necessary, for it is impossible to foretell the exact nature of the difficulties which will confront the pot-holer.
rows.zh: 采取这类预防措施很有必要，因为无法预知探洞者将会遇到的困难究竟是什么样的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The deepest known cave in the world is the Gouffre Berger near Grenoble.
rows.zh: 世界上已知最深的洞穴，是格勒诺布尔附近的贝尔热深洞。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It extends to a depth of 3,723 feet.
rows.zh: 它的深度达到三千七百二十三英尺。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This immense chasm has been formed by an underground stream which has tunnelled a course through a flaw in the rocks.
rows.zh: 这道巨大的深渊是一条地下溪流沿着岩层的一处裂隙冲刷出通道而形成的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The entrance to the cave is on a plateau in the Dauphiné Alps.
rows.zh: 洞口位于多菲内阿尔卑斯山区的一片高原上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As it is only six feet across, it is barely noticeable.
rows.zh: 洞口横宽只有六英尺，几乎看不出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The cave might never have been discovered had not the entrance been spotted by the distinguished French pot-holer, Berger.
rows.zh: 要不是法国著名探洞家贝尔热发现了洞口，这个洞穴也许永远不会被人发现。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Since its discovery, it has become a sort of pot-holers’ Everest.
rows.zh: 自从被发现以来，它便成了探洞者心中某种意义上的珠穆朗玛峰。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though a number of descents have been made, much of it still remains to be explored.
rows.zh: 虽然已有不少人下去探察过，但洞内仍有很大一部分有待探索。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A team of pot-holers recently went down the Gouffre Berger.
rows.zh: 最近，一队探洞者下到了贝尔热深洞。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After entering the narrow gap on the plateau, they climbed down the steep sides of the cave until they came to a narrow corridor.
rows.zh: 他们钻进高原上的狭窄裂口后，沿着陡峭的洞壁往下攀爬，直到来到一条狭窄的通道。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They had to edge their way along this, sometimes wading across shallow streams, or swimming across deep pools.
rows.zh: 他们不得不侧着身子沿通道挪动，有时涉过浅溪，有时游过深潭。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Suddenly they came to a waterfall which dropped into an underground lake at the bottom of the cave.
rows.zh: 突然，他们来到一处瀑布前，瀑布直落洞底的一个地下湖。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They plunged into the lake, and after loading their gear on an inflatable rubber dinghy, let the current carry them to the other side.
rows.zh: 他们跳进湖里，把装备装到一只充气橡皮艇上，任凭水流把他们带到对岸。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: To protect themselves from the icy water, they had to wear special rubber suits.
rows.zh: 为了防止冰冷湖水的侵袭，他们必须穿上特制的橡胶服。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At the far end of the lake, they came to huge piles of rubble which had been washed up by the water.
rows.zh: 到了湖的另一头，他们遇到了被水冲积起来的大堆碎石。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In this part of the cave, they could hear an insistent booming sound which they found was caused by a small waterspout shooting down into a pool from the roof of the cave.
rows.zh: 在洞穴的这一部分，他们听到持续不断的轰鸣，后来发现，这是洞顶的一股细小水柱直冲下面水潭所发出的声音。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Squeezing through a cleft in the rocks, the pot-holers arrived at an enormous cavern, the size of a huge concert hall.
rows.zh: 探洞者从岩石间的一条裂缝挤过去，来到一个庞大的洞厅，大小如同一座巨型音乐厅。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After switching on powerful arc lights, they saw great stalagmites — some of them over forty feet high — rising up like tree-trunks to meet the stalactites suspended from the roof.
rows.zh: 打开强力弧光灯后，他们看到巨大的石笋，有的高达四十多英尺，像树干一样向上伸展，与洞顶垂下的钟乳石相接。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Round about, piles of limestone glistened in all the colours of the rainbow.
rows.zh: 四周成堆的石灰岩闪烁着彩虹般的各种颜色。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the eerie silence of the cavern, the only sound that could be heard was made by water which dripped continuously from the high dome above them.
rows.zh: 洞厅里寂静得有些阴森，唯一听得见的声音，是头顶高高的穹窿上不断滴下的水声。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: fascination 表示强烈的吸引；可说 something has a fascination for someone。
usage.example: For him, caves have the same peculiar fascination which high mountains have for the climber.
usage.exampleZh: 对探洞者来说，洞穴有着一种特殊的吸引力，正如高山之于登山者一样。

rows.en: Insurance companies are normally willing to insure anything.
rows.zh: 保险公司通常什么都愿意承保。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Insuring public or private property is a standard practice in most countries in the world.
rows.zh: 在世界上大多数国家，为公共财产或私人财产投保都是惯常做法。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If, however, you were holding an open air garden party or a fete it would be equally possible to insure yourself in the event of bad weather.
rows.zh: 不过，如果你要举办露天花园聚会或游园会，也同样可以投保，以防遇上坏天气。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Needless to say, the bigger the risk an insurance company takes, the higher the premium you will have to pay.
rows.zh: 不用说，保险公司承担的风险越大，你需要支付的保险费也就越高。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is not uncommon to hear that a shipping company has made a claim for the cost of salvaging a sunken ship.
rows.zh: 听说某家航运公司为打捞沉船的费用提出索赔，并不稀奇。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But the claim made by a local authority to recover the cost of salvaging a sunken pie dish must surely be unique.
rows.zh: 然而，一个地方当局竟为打捞沉入水底的馅饼盘所花的费用索赔，这想必真是独一无二了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Admittedly it was an unusual pie dish, for it was eighteen feet long and six feet wide.
rows.zh: 诚然，这可不是普通的馅饼盘，因为它长十八英尺、宽六英尺。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It had been purchased by a local authority so that an enormous pie could be baked for an annual fair.
rows.zh: 地方当局买下它，是为了给一年一度的集市烤一个巨大的馅饼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The pie committee decided that the best way to transport the dish would be by canal, so they insured it for the trip.
rows.zh: 馅饼筹备委员会认定，用运河运输这个盘子最为合适，于是为这趟运输给它买了保险。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Shortly after it was launched, the pie committee went to a local inn to celebrate.
rows.zh: 盘子下水后不久，委员会的成员就去当地一家小酒馆庆祝。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At the same time, a number of teenagers climbed on to the dish and held a little party of their own.
rows.zh: 与此同时，几个十几岁的少年爬上盘子，自顾自地开起了小聚会。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Dancing proved to be more than the dish could bear, for during the party it capsized and sank in seven feet of water.
rows.zh: 盘子经受不住他们跳舞时的折腾，在聚会中翻了个底朝天，沉到了七英尺深的水底。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The pie committee telephoned a local garage owner who arrived in a recovery truck to salvage the pie dish.
rows.zh: 馅饼委员会给当地一家修车厂的老板打了电话，他开着一辆救援拖车来打捞馅饼盘。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Shivering in their wet clothes, the teenagers looked on while three men dived repeatedly into the water to locate the dish.
rows.zh: 少年们穿着湿衣服，冻得发抖，在旁边看着三个男人反复潜入水中寻找盘子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They had little difficulty in finding it, but hauling it out of the water proved to be a serious problem.
rows.zh: 他们没费多少劲就找到了盘子，但要把它从水里拖出来，却成了个大难题。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The sides of the dish were so smooth that it was almost impossible to attach hawsers and chains to the rim without damaging it.
rows.zh: 盘壁十分光滑，要把粗缆绳和铁链固定在盘边，又不把它弄坏，几乎是不可能的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Eventually chains were fixed to one end of the dish and a powerful winch was put into operation.
rows.zh: 最后，他们把铁链固定在盘子的一端，开动了一台大功率绞车。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The dish rose to the surface and was gently drawn towards the canal bank.
rows.zh: 盘子升到了水面，被缓缓拉向运河岸边。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For one agonizing moment, the dish was perched precariously on the bank of the canal, but it suddenly overbalanced and slid back into the water.
rows.zh: 有那么一瞬间，盘子摇摇欲坠地搁在岸上，令人揪心；但它突然失去平衡，又滑回了水里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The men were now obliged to try once more.
rows.zh: 他们只好再试一次。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This time they fixed heavy metal clamps to both sides of the dish so that they could fasten the chains.
rows.zh: 这一次，他们在盘子两侧装上沉重的金属夹具，以便系牢铁链。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The dish now had to be lifted vertically because one edge was resting against the side of the canal.
rows.zh: 由于一条盘边抵在运河侧壁上，这回必须把盘子竖着吊起来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The winch was again put into operation and one of the men started up the truck.
rows.zh: 绞车再次开动，其中一个人发动了卡车。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Several minutes later, the dish was successfully hauled above the surface of the water.
rows.zh: 几分钟后，盘子终于成功地被吊出了水面。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Water streamed in torrents over its sides with such force that it set up a huge wave in the canal.
rows.zh: 水从盘子四边倾泻而下，力量之大，在运河里激起了一道巨浪。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There was a danger that the wave would rebound off the other side of the bank and send the dish plunging into the water again.
rows.zh: 这道浪有可能撞到对岸后反弹回来，把盘子再度掀进水里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: By working at tremendous speed, the men managed to get the dish on to dry land before the wave returned.
rows.zh: 他们动作飞快，终于赶在浪头回涌前把盘子弄上了干地。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.exampleZh: 在世界上大多数国家，为公共财产或私人财产投保都是惯常做法。

usage.note: of 后接名词；若后接完整句子，可使用 in the event that。
usage.example: If, however, you were holding an open air garden party or a fete it would be equally possible to insure yourself in the event of bad weather.
usage.exampleZh: 不过，如果你要举办露天花园聚会或游园会，也同样可以投保，以防遇上坏天气。

usage.note: claim 在保险语境指索赔，for 后接所要求赔付的费用或损失。
usage.example: It is not uncommon to hear that a shipping company has made a claim for the cost of salvaging a sunken ship.
usage.exampleZh: 听说某家航运公司为打捞沉船的费用提出索赔，并不稀奇。

usage.note: 表示受到情况或责任的迫使；后接动词原形。
usage.example: The men were now obliged to try once more.
usage.exampleZh: 他们只好再试一次。

usage.note: 这里描述启动设备，也可用于实施计划或制度。
usage.example: The winch was again put into operation and one of the men started up the truck.
usage.exampleZh: 绞车再次开动，其中一个人发动了卡车。

rows.en: People travelling long distances frequently have to decide whether they would prefer to go by land, sea, or air.
rows.zh: 长途旅行的人常常必须决定，自己更愿意走陆路、坐船，还是乘飞机。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Hardly anyone can positively enjoy sitting in a train for more than a few hours.
rows.zh: 一连坐上好几个小时的火车，几乎没有谁能真正享受其中。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Train compartments soon get cramped and stuffy.
rows.zh: 火车车厢很快就让人觉得拥挤、闷热。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is almost impossible to take your mind off the journey.
rows.zh: 你几乎不可能把注意力从旅途本身移开。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Reading is only a partial solution, for the monotonous rhythm of the wheels clicking on the rails soon lulls you to sleep.
rows.zh: 阅读只能解决一部分问题，因为车轮在铁轨上咔嗒作响的单调节奏，很快就会把你催入梦乡。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: During the day, sleep comes in snatches.
rows.zh: 白天，你总是断断续续地睡上一会儿。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At night, when you really wish to go to sleep, you rarely manage to do so.
rows.zh: 到了夜里，你真正想睡时，却往往睡不着。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If you are lucky enough to get a sleeper, you spend half the night staring at the small blue light in the ceiling, or fumbling to find your ticket for inspection.
rows.zh: 如果你足够幸运，弄到一张卧铺，半个夜晚也得花在盯着天花板上的小蓝灯，或摸索着寻找车票应付查票上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Inevitably you arrive at your destination almost exhausted.
rows.zh: 到达目的地时，你免不了已精疲力竭。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Long car journeys are even less pleasant, for it is quite impossible even to read.
rows.zh: 坐汽车长途旅行就更不愉快了，因为连看书都完全不可能。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: On motorways you can, at least, travel fairly safely at high speeds, but more often than not, the greater part of the journey is spent on roads with few service stations and too much traffic.
rows.zh: 在高速公路上，你至少还能相当安全地高速行驶；但大多数时候，旅程的大部分是在服务站寥寥无几、车辆却太多的道路上度过的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: By comparison, ferry trips or cruises offer a great variety of civilized comforts.
rows.zh: 相形之下，乘渡轮或坐游轮能让人享受到各种体面舒适的便利。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: You can stretch your legs on the spacious decks, play games, meet interesting people and enjoy good food — always assuming, of course, that the sea is calm.
rows.zh: 你可以在宽敞的甲板上活动腿脚、玩游戏、结识有趣的人、享用美食——当然，这一切始终得以海面平静为前提。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If it is not, and you are likely to get seasick, no form of transport could be worse.
rows.zh: 如果海面不平静，而你又容易晕船，那就没有比这更糟的交通方式了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even if you travel in ideal weather, sea journeys take a long time.
rows.zh: 即使天气理想，海上旅程也很耗时。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Relatively few people are prepared to sacrifice holiday time for the pleasure of travelling by sea.
rows.zh: 愿意为了乘船的乐趣而牺牲假期时间的人，相对来说很少。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Aeroplanes have the reputation of being dangerous and even hardened travellers are intimidated by them.
rows.zh: 飞机素有危险之名，连久经旅途的老手也对它心存畏惧。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They also have the disadvantage of being an expensive form of transport.
rows.zh: 它还有一个缺点，就是费用高昂。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But nothing can match them for speed and comfort.
rows.zh: 但论速度和舒适程度，没有什么能比得上飞机。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Travelling at a height of 30,000 feet, far above the clouds, and at over 500 miles an hour is an exhilarating experience.
rows.zh: 在远高于云层的三万英尺高空，以每小时五百多英里的速度飞行，是一种令人振奋的体验。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: You do not have to devise ways of taking your mind off the journey, for an aeroplane gets you to your destination rapidly.
rows.zh: 你不必费心设法把注意力从旅途上移开，因为飞机很快就把你送到目的地了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For a few hours, you settle back in a deep armchair to enjoy the flight.
rows.zh: 几个小时里，你舒舒服服地靠在宽大的扶手椅上，享受飞行。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The real escapist can watch a film and sip champagne on some services.
rows.zh: 在某些航班上，真正想暂时逃离现实的人，还可以一边看电影，一边小口品着香槟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But even when such refinements are not available, there is plenty to keep you occupied.
rows.zh: 即使没有这些精致享受，也有足够多的事情让你消磨时间。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: An aeroplane offers you an unusual and breathtaking view of the world.
rows.zh: 飞机让你以不同寻常、令人屏息的视角俯瞰世界。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: You soar effortlessly over high mountains and deep valleys.
rows.zh: 你毫不费力地飞越高山深谷。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: You really see the shape of the land.
rows.zh: 你能真切地看到大地的形状。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If the landscape is hidden from view, you can enjoy the extraordinary sight of unbroken cloud plains that stretch out for miles before you, while the sun shines brilliantly in a clear sky.
rows.zh: 如果地面景色被遮住，你还可以欣赏连绵数英里的壮观云海，在你眼前铺展，而太阳正在晴朗的天空中灿烂地照耀。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The journey is so smooth that there is nothing to prevent you from reading or sleeping.
rows.zh: 旅途平稳得很，没有什么会妨碍你阅读或睡觉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: However you decide to spend your time, one thing is certain: you will arrive at your destination fresh and uncrumpled.
rows.zh: 无论你决定怎样打发时间，有一点是肯定的：你到达目的地时，会精神饱满、衣着平整。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: You will not have to spend the next few days recovering from a long and arduous journey.
rows.zh: 你不必再用接下来的几天时间，从一次漫长而艰苦的旅程中恢复过来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: off 后接让人烦心或难以忘怀的事情；所有格随主语变化。
usage.example: It is almost impossible to take your mind off the journey.
usage.exampleZh: 你几乎不可能把注意力从旅途本身移开。

usage.meaning: 断断续续地；一阵一阵地
usage.note: 常与 sleep 等搭配，表示时间短促且不连续。
usage.example: During the day, sleep comes in snatches.
usage.exampleZh: 白天，你总是断断续续地睡上一会儿。

usage.note: 整体表示经常发生，不能逐词理解成对次数的简单否定。
usage.example: On motorways you can, at least, travel fairly safely at high speeds, but more often than not, the greater part of the journey is spent on roads with few service stations and too much traffic.
usage.exampleZh: 在高速公路上，你至少还能相当安全地高速行驶；但大多数时候，旅程的大部分是在服务站寥寥无几、车辆却太多的道路上度过的。

usage.note: 常用于坐进椅子里准备休息或享受某事的情景。
usage.example: For a few hours, you settle back in a deep armchair to enjoy the flight.
usage.exampleZh: 几个小时里，你舒舒服服地靠在宽大的扶手椅上，享受飞行。

usage.note: from 引出疾病、劳累或打击等需要恢复的原因。
usage.example: You will not have to spend the next few days recovering from a long and arduous journey.
usage.exampleZh: 你不必再用接下来的几天时间，从一次漫长而艰苦的旅程中恢复过来。

rows.en: In democratic countries any efforts to restrict the freedom of the press are rightly condemned.
rows.zh: 在民主国家，任何限制新闻自由的企图都会受到谴责，这样的谴责是正当的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: However, this freedom can easily be abused.
rows.zh: 不过，这种自由很容易被滥用。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Stories about people often attract far more public attention than political events.
rows.zh: 有关人物的报道所吸引的公众注意，往往远远超过政治事件。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though we may enjoy reading about the lives of others, it is extremely doubtful whether we would equally enjoy reading about ourselves.
rows.zh: 我们也许喜欢读别人的生活故事，可如果读到的是自己的生活，是否还会同样高兴，就很值得怀疑了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Acting on the contention that facts are sacred, reporters can cause untold suffering to individuals by publishing details about their private lives.
rows.zh: 记者奉行“事实神圣不可侵犯”的主张，把个人私生活的细节公之于众，可能给当事人造成无法言尽的痛苦。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Newspapers exert such tremendous influence that they can not only bring about major changes to the lives of ordinary people but can even overthrow a government.
rows.zh: 报纸的影响力如此巨大，不仅能使普通人的生活发生重大变化，甚至能推翻一个政府。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The story of a poor family that acquired fame and fortune overnight, dramatically illustrates the power of the press.
rows.zh: 有个穷困家庭一夜之间名利双收，它的故事鲜明地显示了新闻界的力量。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The family lived in Aberdeen, a small town of 23,000 inhabitants in South Dakota.
rows.zh: 这家人住在南达科他州的阿伯丁，那是一个有两万三千名居民的小镇。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As the parents had five children, life was a perpetual struggle against poverty.
rows.zh: 父母已经有五个孩子，因此生活始终是在贫困中挣扎。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They were expecting their sixth child and were faced with even more pressing economic problems.
rows.zh: 他们正等着第六个孩子出生，面临着更加迫切的经济难题。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If they had only had one more child, the fact would have passed unnoticed.
rows.zh: 如果他们只是再添一个孩子，这件事本来不会引起任何注意。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They would have continued to struggle against economic odds and would have lived in obscurity.
rows.zh: 他们本会继续在经济困境中苦苦支撑，默默无闻地生活下去。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But they suddenly became the parents of quintuplets, four girls and a boy, an event which radically changed their lives.
rows.zh: 然而，他们突然成了五胞胎的父母——四个女孩和一个男孩；这件事彻底改变了他们的生活。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The day after the birth of the five children, an aeroplane arrived in Aberdeen bringing sixty reporters and photographers.
rows.zh: 五个孩子出生后的第二天，一架飞机带着六十名记者和摄影师来到了阿伯丁。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The rise to fame was swift.
rows.zh: 他们迅速成了名人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Television cameras and newspapers carried the news to everyone in the country.
rows.zh: 电视摄像机和报纸把这条消息传给了全国每一个人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Newspapers and magazines offered the family huge sums for the exclusive rights to publish stories and photographs.
rows.zh: 报纸和杂志愿意付给这家人巨额报酬，以获得独家刊登报道和照片的权利。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Gifts poured in not only from unknown people, but from baby food and soap manufacturers who wished to advertise their products.
rows.zh: 礼物源源不断地涌来，不仅来自素不相识的人，也来自想为产品做广告的婴儿食品和肥皂制造商。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The old farmhouse the family lived in was to be replaced by a new $500,000 home.
rows.zh: 这家人住的旧农舍，将被一栋价值五十万美元的新住宅所取代。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Reporters kept pressing for interviews so lawyers had to be employed to act as spokesmen for the family at press conferences.
rows.zh: 记者不断要求采访，因此他们不得不雇用律师，在新闻发布会上充当这个家庭的发言人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: While the five babies were still quietly sleeping in oxygen tents in a hospital nursery, their parents were paying the price for fame.
rows.zh: 五个婴儿还在医院育婴室的氧气帐里安静地睡着，父母却已经在为出名付出代价了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It would never again be possible for them to lead normal lives.
rows.zh: 从此，他们再也不可能过正常的生活。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They had become the victims of commercialization, for their names had acquired a market value.
rows.zh: 他们成了商业化的受害者，因为他们的名字已经有了市场价值。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Instead of being five new family members, these children had immediately become a commodity.
rows.zh: 这五个孩子一出生就成了商品，而不再只是家里新添的五个成员。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 后面接变化或结果，强调促成其发生。
usage.example: Newspapers exert such tremendous influence that they can not only bring about major changes to the lives of ordinary people but can even overthrow a government.
usage.exampleZh: 报纸的影响力如此巨大，不仅能使普通人的生活发生重大变化，甚至能推翻一个政府。

usage.note: 常用于 acquire、achieve、seek 等动词后，表示名利双收或追求名利。
usage.example: The story of a poor family that acquired fame and fortune overnight, dramatically illustrates the power of the press.
usage.exampleZh: 有个穷困家庭一夜之间名利双收，它的故事鲜明地显示了新闻界的力量。

usage.note: obscurity 在这里指不为人知，不是光线昏暗。
usage.example: They would have continued to struggle against economic odds and would have lived in obscurity.
usage.exampleZh: 他们本会继续在经济困境中苦苦支撑，默默无闻地生活下去。

usage.note: 常用于礼物、消息、捐款等接连到来，主语通常是涌来的事物。
usage.example: Gifts poured in not only from unknown people, but from baby food and soap manufacturers who wished to advertise their products.
usage.exampleZh: 礼物源源不断地涌来，不仅来自素不相识的人，也来自想为产品做广告的婴儿食品和肥皂制造商。

usage.note: 这里是比喻用法，price 不一定指金钱；for 后接付出代价的缘由。
usage.example: While the five babies were still quietly sleeping in oxygen tents in a hospital nursery, their parents were paying the price for fame.
usage.exampleZh: 五个婴儿还在医院育婴室的氧气帐里安静地睡着，父母却已经在为出名付出代价了。

rows.en: So great is our passion for doing things for ourselves, that we are becoming increasingly less dependent on specialized labour.
rows.zh: 我们对自己动手做事的热情如此高涨，以至于对专业工人的依赖正日益减少。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: No one can plead ignorance of a subject any longer, for there are countless do-it-yourself publications.
rows.zh: 现在谁也不能再借口说自己对某个领域一无所知，因为教人自己动手的出版物多得数不清。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Armed with the right tools and materials, newlyweds gaily embark on the task of decorating their own homes.
rows.zh: 新婚夫妇备齐合适的工具和材料，便兴致勃勃地开始装修自己的家。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Men, particularly, spend hours of their leisure time installing their own fireplaces, laying out their own gardens; building garages and making furniture.
rows.zh: 尤其是男人，会花上许多闲暇时间，自己安装壁炉、布置花园、盖车库、做家具。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Some really keen enthusiasts go so far as to build their own computers.
rows.zh: 有些格外痴迷的爱好者，甚至连电脑也自己组装。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Shops cater for the do-it-yourself craze not only by running special advisory services for novices, but by offering consumers bits and pieces which they can assemble at home.
rows.zh: 商店为迎合这股自己动手的热潮，不仅为新手提供专门的咨询服务，还向顾客出售可以带回家自行组装的各种零部件。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Such things provide an excellent outlet for pent up creative energy, but unfortunately not all of us are born handymen.
rows.zh: 这些活动为积蓄已久的创造力提供了绝佳的释放途径，但遗憾的是，并非人人天生都有一双巧手。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Some wives tend to believe that their husbands are infinitely resourceful and can fix anything.
rows.zh: 有些妻子总以为丈夫有无穷的办法，什么都修得好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even men who can hardly drive a nail in straight are supposed to be born electricians, carpenters, plumbers and mechanics.
rows.zh: 就连那些几乎连钉子都钉不直的男人，也被当成天生的电工、木匠、水管工和机械修理工。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When lights fuse, furniture gets rickety, pipes get clogged, or vacuum cleaners fail to operate, some women assume that their husbands will somehow put things right.
rows.zh: 灯的保险丝烧断了，家具摇晃了，管子堵了，或者吸尘器不工作了，有些女人就认定丈夫总能想办法修好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The worst thing about the do-it-yourself game is that sometimes even men live under the delusion that they can do anything, even when they have repeatedly been proved wrong.
rows.zh: 自己动手这件事最糟糕的一点，是有时连男人自己也误以为什么都能干，哪怕事实已经一再证明他们错了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is a question of pride as much as anything else.
rows.zh: 这很大程度上也是个面子问题。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Last spring my wife suggested that I call in a man to look at our lawn mower.
rows.zh: 去年春天，妻子提议叫个人来看看我们的割草机。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It had broken down the previous summer, and though I promised to repair it, I had never got round to it.
rows.zh: 它前一年夏天就坏了；我虽然答应修，却始终没抽出时间来动手。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I would not hear of the suggestion and said that I would fix it myself.
rows.zh: 我坚决不接受这个建议，说要自己把它修好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One Saturday afternoon, I hauled the machine into the garden and had a close look at it.
rows.zh: 一个星期六的下午，我把机器拖到花园里，仔细检查了一番。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As far as I could see, it needed only a minor adjustment: a turn of a screw here, a little tightening up there, a drop of oil and it would be as good as new.
rows.zh: 在我看来，它只需要稍作调整：这里拧一下螺丝，那里紧一紧，再滴一点油，就能像新的一样了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Inevitably the repair job was not quite so simple.
rows.zh: 不出所料，修理起来并没有那么简单。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The mower firmly refused to mow, so I decided to dismantle it.
rows.zh: 割草机就是不肯割草，我于是决定把它拆开。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The garden was soon littered with chunks of metal which had once made up a lawn mower.
rows.zh: 不一会儿，花园里就散落着大块大块的金属零件，它们原先合在一起就是一台割草机。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But I was extremely pleased with myself.
rows.zh: 可我却对自己十分满意。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I had traced the cause of the trouble.
rows.zh: 我已经找出了故障的原因。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One of the links in the chain that drives the wheels had snapped.
rows.zh: 驱动车轮的链条上，有一节链环断了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After buying a new chain I was faced with the insurmountable task of putting the confusing jigsaw puzzle together again.
rows.zh: 买来新链条后，我却面临着一个无法完成的任务：把这堆令人眼花缭乱的拼图再拼回去。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I was not surprised to find that the machine still refused to work after I had reassembled it, for the simple reason that I was left with several curiously shaped bits of metal which did not seem to fit anywhere.
rows.zh: 重新装好后，机器仍不肯工作，我对此并不惊讶，原因很简单：我面前还剩着几块形状古怪的金属零件，似乎哪儿都装不上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I gave up in despair.
rows.zh: 我绝望地放弃了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The weeks passed and the grass grew.
rows.zh: 几个星期过去，草也长高了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When my wife nagged me to do something about it, I told her that either I would have to buy a new mower or let the grass grow.
rows.zh: 妻子唠叨着让我想想办法，我告诉她，要么得买台新割草机，要么就任草长下去。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Needless to say our house is now surrounded by a jungle.
rows.zh: 不用说，我们家如今已经被一片丛林包围了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Buried somewhere in deep grass there is a rusting lawn mower which I have promised to repair one day.
rows.zh: 在深深的草丛某处，埋着一台正在生锈的割草机，而我还答应着总有一天把它修好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 常用于开始一项重要或需花费精力的任务、事业或旅程。
usage.example: Armed with the right tools and materials, newlyweds gaily embark on the task of decorating their own homes.
usage.exampleZh: 新婚夫妇备齐合适的工具和材料，便兴致勃勃地开始装修自己的家。

usage.meaning: 零零碎碎的东西；各种零部件
usage.note: 固定并列短语，既可指小物件，也可指零星的信息。
usage.example: Shops cater for the do-it-yourself craze not only by running special advisory services for novices, but by offering consumers bits and pieces which they can assemble at home.
usage.exampleZh: 商店为迎合这股自己动手的热潮，不仅为新手提供专门的咨询服务，还向顾客出售可以带回家自行组装的各种零部件。

usage.meaning: 把问题解决；把东西修好
usage.note: right 在这里表示恢复正常，也可用于纠正错误或弥补局面。
usage.example: When lights fuse, furniture gets rickety, pipes get clogged, or vacuum cleaners fail to operate, some women assume that their husbands will somehow put things right.
usage.exampleZh: 灯的保险丝烧断了，家具摇晃了，管子堵了，或者吸尘器不工作了，有些女人就认定丈夫总能想办法修好。

usage.note: to 是介词，后接名词或动名词；常用于拖延后才着手的事情。
usage.example: It had broken down the previous summer, and though I promised to repair it, I had never got round to it.
usage.exampleZh: 它前一年夏天就坏了；我虽然答应修，却始终没抽出时间来动手。

usage.note: 常作状语说明人的心境，despair 是不可数名词。
usage.example: I gave up in despair.
usage.exampleZh: 我绝望地放弃了。

rows.en: Pollution is the price we pay for an overpopulated, over-industrialized planet.
rows.zh: 污染，是我们为一个人口过多、工业化过度的地球所付出的代价。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When you come to think about it, there are only four ways you can deal with rubbish: dump it, burn it, turn it into something you can use again, attempt to produce less of it.
rows.zh: 仔细想来，处理垃圾只有四种办法：倾倒、焚烧、把它变成可再次利用的东西，以及设法少制造一些。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We keep trying all four methods, but the sheer volume of rubbish we produce worldwide threatens to overwhelm us.
rows.zh: 这四种办法我们一直都在尝试，但全世界制造出来的垃圾数量实在太大，几乎要把我们淹没。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Rubbish, however, is only part of the problem of polluting our planet.
rows.zh: 然而，垃圾只是地球污染问题的一部分。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The need to produce ever-increasing quantities of cheap food leads to a different kind of pollution.
rows.zh: 人们需要生产数量不断增长的廉价食物，这又导致了另一种污染。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Industrialized farming methods produce cheap meat products: beef, pork and chicken.
rows.zh: 工业化的养殖方法带来了廉价的肉类产品：牛肉、猪肉和鸡肉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The use of pesticides and fertilizers produces cheap grain and vegetables.
rows.zh: 使用农药和化肥，带来了廉价的粮食和蔬菜。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The price we pay for cheap food may be already too high: Mad Cow Disease (BSE) in cattle, salmonella in chicken and eggs, and listeria in dairy products.
rows.zh: 我们为廉价食物付出的代价，也许早已过高：牛身上的疯牛病，即牛海绵状脑病，鸡肉和鸡蛋中的沙门氏菌，以及乳制品中的李斯特菌。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And if you think you'll abandon meat and become a vegetarian, you have the choice of very expensive organically-grown vegetables or a steady diet of pesticides every time you think you're eating fresh salads and vegetables, or just having an innocent glass of water!
rows.zh: 而如果你打算不再吃肉，改做素食者，那么摆在面前的选择是：要么吃价格极高的有机蔬菜，要么每次自以为在吃新鲜沙拉和蔬菜，甚至只是喝一杯本以为无害的水时，都在不断摄入农药！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: However, there is an even more insidious kind of pollution that particularly affects urban areas and invades our daily lives, and that is noise.
rows.zh: 然而，还有一种更为隐蔽的污染，尤其影响城市地区，侵入我们的日常生活，那就是噪声。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Burglar alarms going off at any time of the day or night serve only to annoy passers-by and actually assist burglars to burgle.
rows.zh: 防盗警报不分昼夜地响起，只能惹得路人烦躁，实际上倒帮了窃贼行窃。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Car alarms constantly scream at us in the street and are a source of profound irritation.
rows.zh: 汽车警报在街上不停地对着我们尖叫，让人极其恼火。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A recent survey of the effects of noise revealed (surprisingly?)
rows.zh: 最近一项关于噪声影响的调查揭示了这样一个结果（意外吗？）：
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: that dogs barking incessantly in the night rated the highest form of noise pollution on a scale ranging from 1 to 7.
rows.zh: 在一到七级的评定尺度上，夜间不停的狗叫声被评为最严重的噪声污染。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The survey revealed a large number of sources of noise that we really dislike.
rows.zh: 调查列出了大量我们确实厌恶的噪声来源。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Lawn mowers whining on a summer’s day, late-night parties in apartment blocks, noisy neighbours, vehicles of all kinds, especially large container trucks thundering through quiet villages, planes and helicopters flying overhead, large radios carried round in public places and played at maximum volume.
rows.zh: 夏日里嗡嗡作响的割草机，公寓楼内深夜的聚会，吵闹的邻居，各种车辆，尤其是轰隆隆驶过宁静村庄的大型集装箱卡车，头顶飞过的飞机和直升机，还有人们带到公共场所、把音量开到最大的大收音机。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: New technology has also made its own contribution to noise.
rows.zh: 新技术也为噪声作出了自己的“贡献”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A lot of people object to mobile phones, especially when they are used in public places like restaurants or on public transport.
rows.zh: 很多人反感手机，尤其反感人们在餐馆或公共交通工具上等公共场所使用手机。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Loud conversations on mobile phones invade our thoughts or interrupt the pleasure of meeting friends for a quiet chat.
rows.zh: 用手机大声交谈，会侵扰我们的思绪，或打断与朋友安静聊天的乐趣。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The noise pollution survey revealed a rather surprising and possibly amusing old-fashioned source of noise.
rows.zh: 这次噪声污染调查还发现了一种相当出人意料、也许还颇为好笑的老式噪声来源。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It turned out to be snoring!
rows.zh: 结果竟然是打鼾！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Men were found to be the worst offenders.
rows.zh: 调查发现，男人是最严重的制造者。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was revealed that 20% of men in their mid-thirties snore.
rows.zh: 调查表明，三十五岁左右的男性中，有百分之二十打鼾。
rows.speaker: 旁白
