rows.en: This figure rises to a staggering 60% of men in their sixties.
rows.zh: 到了六十多岁的男性中，这个比例上升到惊人的百分之六十。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Against these figures, it was found that only 5% of women snore regularly, while the rest are constantly woken or kept awake by their trumpeting partners.
rows.zh: 相比之下，只有百分之五的女性经常打鼾，其余女性却常被伴侣喇叭般的鼾声吵醒，或吵得无法入睡。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Whatever the source of noise, one thing is certain: silence, it seems, has become a golden memory.
rows.zh: 不管噪声来自哪里，有一点是肯定的：寂静似乎已成为珍贵的回忆。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 用来引出经过考虑后注意到的一点，常放在从句或插入语中。
usage.example: When you come to think about it, there are only four ways you can deal with rubbish: dump it, burn it, turn it into something you can use again, attempt to produce less of it.
usage.exampleZh: 仔细想来，处理垃圾只有四种办法：倾倒、焚烧、把它变成可再次利用的东西，以及设法少制造一些。

usage.note: 警报、闹钟等作主语时，go off 指发出响声，并非停止工作。
usage.example: Burglar alarms going off at any time of the day or night serve only to annoy passers-by and actually assist burglars to burgle.
usage.exampleZh: 防盗警报不分昼夜地响起，只能惹得路人烦躁，实际上倒帮了窃贼行窃。

usage.note: to 是介词，后接名词或动名词；名词 object 的读音和动词不同。
usage.example: A lot of people object to mobile phones, especially when they are used in public places like restaurants or on public transport.
usage.exampleZh: 很多人反感手机，尤其反感人们在餐馆或公共交通工具上等公共场所使用手机。

usage.note: 用来说明后来查明的实际情况，往往带意外意味。
usage.example: It turned out to be snoring!
usage.exampleZh: 结果竟然是打鼾！

usage.note: awake 是形容词，置于宾语之后；本例为被动形式。
usage.example: Against these figures, it was found that only 5% of women snore regularly, while the rest are constantly woken or kept awake by their trumpeting partners.
usage.exampleZh: 相比之下，只有百分之五的女性经常打鼾，其余女性却常被伴侣喇叭般的鼾声吵醒，或吵得无法入睡。

rows.en: In this much-travelled world, there are still thousands of places which are inaccessible to tourists.
rows.zh: 如今世界各地人们频繁旅行，却仍有成千上万个地方是游客无法到达的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We always assume that villagers in remote places are friendly and hospitable.
rows.zh: 我们总以为，偏远地方的村民都友善好客。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But people who are cut off not only from foreign tourists, but even from their own countrymen can be hostile to travellers.
rows.zh: 然而，有些人不仅与外国游客隔绝，甚至与本国其他人也少有往来，他们可能会对旅人怀有敌意。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Visits to really remote villages are seldom enjoyable — as my wife and I discovered during a tour through the Balkans.
rows.zh: 游览真正偏僻的村庄，很少是件愉快的事；我和妻子在穿行巴尔干地区的一次旅行中，就发现了这一点。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We had spent several days in a small town and visited a number of old churches in the vicinity.
rows.zh: 我们在一个小镇住了几天，游览了附近好几座古老的教堂。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: These attracted many visitors, for they were not only of great architectural interest, but contained a large number of beautifully preserved frescoes as well.
rows.zh: 这些教堂吸引了许多游客，因为它们不仅在建筑上很有观赏价值，里面还保存着大量完好的精美壁画。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: On the day before our departure, several bus loads of tourists descended on the town.
rows.zh: 在我们离开的前一天，几大车游客涌进了镇子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This was more than we could bear, so we decided to spend our last day exploring the countryside.
rows.zh: 这实在让我们受不了，于是我们决定，把最后一天用来探索乡间。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Taking a path which led out of the town, we crossed a few fields until we came to a dense wood.
rows.zh: 我们沿一条通往镇外的小路，穿过几块田地，来到一片茂密的树林。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We expected the path to end abruptly, but we found that it traced its way through the trees.
rows.zh: 我们以为小路会就此突然中断，却发现它继续蜿蜒穿过树林。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We tramped through the wood for over two hours until we arrived at a deep stream.
rows.zh: 我们在林中跋涉了两个多小时，来到一条水很深的溪流旁。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We could see that the path continued on the other side, but we had no idea how we could get across the stream.
rows.zh: 我们看得见小路在对岸继续延伸，却不知道怎样才能过溪。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Suddenly my wife spotted a boat moored to the bank.
rows.zh: 突然，妻子发现岸边泊着一条船。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In it there was a boatman fast asleep.
rows.zh: 船里有个船夫正睡得很熟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We gently woke him up and asked him to ferry us to the other side.
rows.zh: 我们轻轻叫醒他，请他把我们渡到对岸。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though he was reluctant to do so at first, we eventually persuaded him to take us.
rows.zh: 他起初不大愿意，但我们最后还是说服他载我们过去了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The path led to a tiny village perched on the steep sides of a mountain.
rows.zh: 小路通向一个小村庄，村子依在陡峭的山坡上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The place consisted of a straggling unmade road which was lined on either side by small houses.
rows.zh: 村里只有一条弯曲散漫、未经铺修的道路，两旁排列着小房子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even under a clear blue sky, the village looked forbidding, as all the houses were built of grey mud bricks.
rows.zh: 所有房屋都是灰色土坯砌成的，因而即便头顶是明净的蓝天，整个村子仍显得阴沉得令人却步。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The village seemed deserted, the only sign of life being an ugly-looking black goat on a short length of rope tied to a tree in a field nearby.
rows.zh: 村子仿佛空无一人，唯一有生命的迹象，是附近田里一只丑陋的黑山羊，用一截短绳拴在树上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Sitting down on a dilapidated wooden fence near the field, we opened a couple of tins of sardines and had a picnic lunch.
rows.zh: 我们在田边一道破旧的木栅栏上坐下，打开几罐沙丁鱼，吃了一顿野餐午饭。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All at once, I noticed that my wife seemed to be filled with alarm.
rows.zh: 突然，我注意到妻子似乎满脸惊恐。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Looking up I saw that we were surrounded by children in rags who were looking at us silently as we ate.
rows.zh: 抬头一看，我发现一群衣衫褴褛的孩子围在我们身边，默默地看着我们吃东西。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We offered them food and spoke to them kindly, but they remained motionless.
rows.zh: 我们把食物递给他们，和气地同他们说话，他们却仍一动不动。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I concluded that they were simply shy of strangers.
rows.zh: 我认定，他们只是怕生罢了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When we later walked down the main street of the village, we were followed by a silent procession of children.
rows.zh: 后来我们沿着村里的大街走去，一队默不作声的孩子跟在我们后面。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The village which had seemed deserted, immediately came to life.
rows.zh: 刚才似乎空无一人的村庄，一下子活了过来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Faces appeared at windows.
rows.zh: 窗口出现了一张张面孔。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Men in shirt sleeves stood outside their houses and glared at us.
rows.zh: 只穿着衬衣的男人站在屋外，怒目瞪着我们。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Old women in black shawls peered at us from doorways.
rows.zh: 披着黑色披肩的老妇人从门口探头望着我们。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The most frightening thing of all was that not a sound could be heard.
rows.zh: 最吓人的是，竟然听不到一点声音。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There was no doubt that we were unwelcome visitors.
rows.zh: 毫无疑问，我们是不受欢迎的来客。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We needed no further warning.
rows.zh: 我们不需要再有什么警告了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Turning back down the main street, we quickened our pace and made our way rapidly towards the stream where we hoped the boatman was waiting.
rows.zh: 我们沿大街掉头往回走，加快脚步，迅速朝溪流赶去，希望船夫还在那里等着。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.matchedForm: are cut off not only from
usage.note: cut off 与 from 构成搭配；本例插入 not only，说明隔绝不止一种对象。
usage.example: But people who are cut off not only from foreign tourists, but even from their own countrymen can be hostile to travellers.
usage.exampleZh: 然而，有些人不仅与外国游客隔绝，甚至与本国其他人也少有往来，他们可能会对旅人怀有敌意。

usage.note: fast 在这里表示睡得很沉，不表示速度快；常作表语或补语。
usage.example: In it there was a boatman fast asleep.
usage.exampleZh: 船里有个船夫正睡得很熟。

usage.note: 在这里相当于 suddenly；其他语境中也可表示同时。
usage.example: All at once, I noticed that my wife seemed to be filled with alarm.
usage.exampleZh: 突然，我注意到妻子似乎满脸惊恐。

usage.note: 既可形容地方突然热闹，也可指故事或人物被生动呈现。
usage.example: The village which had seemed deserted, immediately came to life.
usage.exampleZh: 刚才似乎空无一人的村庄，一下子活了过来。

usage.note: that 后接完整句子，用来表达确定的判断。
usage.example: There was no doubt that we were unwelcome visitors.
usage.exampleZh: 毫无疑问，我们是不受欢迎的来客。

rows.en: It is a good thing my aunt Harriet died years ago.
rows.zh: 幸好我的哈丽特姨妈多年前就去世了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If she were alive today she would not be able to air her views on her favourite topic of conversation: domestic servants.
rows.zh: 假如她今天还活着，就没法再就她最爱谈的话题——家佣——发表高论了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Aunt Harriet lived in that leisurely age when servants were employed to do housework.
rows.zh: 哈丽特姨妈生活在那个悠闲的年代，那时人们会雇佣仆人料理家务。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She had a huge, rambling country house called ‘The Gables’.
rows.zh: 她有一栋占地宽广、房间错落延伸的乡间大宅，名叫“山墙庄园”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She was sentimentally attached to this house, for even though it was far too big for her needs, she persisted in living there long after her husband’s death.
rows.zh: 她对这房子有深厚的感情；尽管房子远远大于她实际所需，丈夫去世很久以后，她仍执意住在那里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Before she grew old, Aunt Harriet used to entertain lavishly.
rows.zh: 哈丽特姨妈年纪还不大时，经常大摆筵席招待客人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I often visited The Gables when I was a boy.
rows.zh: 我小时候常去山墙庄园。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: No matter how many guests were present, the great house was always immaculate.
rows.zh: 无论来了多少客人，大宅里总是一尘不染。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The parquet floors shone like mirrors; highly polished silver was displayed in gleaming glass cabinets; even my uncle’s huge collection of books was kept miraculously free from dust.
rows.zh: 拼花地板亮如镜面；擦得锃亮的银器陈列在闪闪发光的玻璃柜里；就连姨父数量庞大的藏书，也奇迹般地毫无灰尘。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Aunt Harriet presided over an invisible army of servants that continuously scrubbed, cleaned, and polished.
rows.zh: 哈丽特姨妈统领着一支看不见的仆人大军，他们不停地刷洗、清扫、擦亮各种东西。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She always referred to them as ‘the shifting population’, for they came and went with such frequency that I never even got a chance to learn their names.
rows.zh: 她总称他们为“流动人口”，因为他们来来去去太频繁，我甚至都没有机会记住他们的名字。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though my aunt pursued what was, in those days, an enlightened policy, in that she never allowed her domestic staff to work more than eight hours a day, she was extremely difficult to please.
rows.zh: 姨妈从不让家佣每天工作超过八小时，这在当年算得上开明的做法，可她却极难伺候得满意。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: While she always criticized the fickleness of human nature, she carried on an unrelenting search for the ideal servant to the end of her days, even after she had been sadly disillusioned by Bessie.
rows.zh: 她一面总是批评人性反复无常，一面又从不放弃寻找理想仆人，直到生命的最后一天；即使贝茜曾让她的幻想痛苦地破灭，她也仍是如此。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Bessie worked for Aunt Harriet for three years.
rows.zh: 贝茜给哈丽特姨妈做了三年事。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: During that time she so gained my aunt’s confidence, that she was put in charge of the domestic staff.
rows.zh: 在那段时间里，她深得姨妈信任，以至于被任命为家佣的主管。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Aunt Harriet could not find words to praise Bessie’s industriousness and efficiency.
rows.zh: 哈丽特姨妈对贝茜的勤劳和办事效率，简直赞不绝口。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In addition to all her other qualifications, Bessie was an expert cook.
rows.zh: 除了其他种种长处，贝茜还是一位烹饪能手。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She acted the role of the perfect servant for three years before Aunt Harriet discovered her ‘little weakness’.
rows.zh: 她扮演了三年的完美仆人之后，哈丽特姨妈才发现了她那点“小毛病”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After being absent from The Gables for a week, my aunt unexpectedly returned one afternoon with a party of guests and instructed Bessie to prepare dinner.
rows.zh: 姨妈离开山墙庄园一个星期后，一天下午突然带着一群客人回来，吩咐贝茜准备晚餐。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Not only was the meal well below the usual standard, but Bessie seemed unable to walk steadily.
rows.zh: 那顿饭不仅远低于平日的水准，连贝茜走起路来也似乎摇摇晃晃。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She bumped into the furniture and kept mumbling about the guests.
rows.zh: 她一会儿撞到家具，一会儿又不停含糊地嘟囔着客人的事。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When she came in with the last course — a huge pudding — she tripped on the carpet and the pudding went flying through the air, narrowly missed my aunt, and crashed on the dining table with considerable force.
rows.zh: 端着最后一道菜——一个巨大的布丁——进来时，她被地毯绊了一跤，布丁飞上半空，险些砸中姨妈，最后重重地摔在餐桌上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though this caused great mirth among the guests, Aunt Harriet was horrified.
rows.zh: 客人们为此乐不可支，哈丽特姨妈却吓坏了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She reluctantly came to the conclusion that Bessie was drunk.
rows.zh: 她不得不承认一个自己不愿接受的结论：贝茜喝醉了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The guests had, of course, realized this from the moment Bessie opened the door for them and, long before the final catastrophe, had had a difficult time trying to conceal their amusement.
rows.zh: 当然，贝茜替客人开门的那一刻，他们就已明白了这一点；远在最后那场灾难发生之前，他们就已经忍笑忍得很辛苦了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The poor girl was dismissed instantly.
rows.zh: 这个可怜的姑娘立刻被辞退了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After her departure, Aunt Harriet discovered that there were piles of empty wine bottles of all shapes and sizes neatly stacked in what had once been Bessie’s wardrobe.
rows.zh: 她离开后，哈丽特姨妈发现，在贝茜原来的衣柜里，整整齐齐地码着成堆的空酒瓶，形状大小各不相同。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They had mysteriously found their way there from the wine cellar!
rows.zh: 它们竟然神不知鬼不觉地从酒窖里跑到了这里！
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: air 在这里是动词，表示公开表达意见；所有格随主语变化。
usage.example: If she were alive today she would not be able to air her views on her favourite topic of conversation: domestic servants.
usage.exampleZh: 假如她今天还活着，就没法再就她最爱谈的话题——家佣——发表高论了。

usage.note: in 后接名词或动名词，往往带不因困难或反对而改变的意味。
usage.example: She was sentimentally attached to this house, for even though it was far too big for her needs, she persisted in living there long after her husband’s death.
usage.exampleZh: 她对这房子有深厚的感情；尽管房子远远大于她实际所需，丈夫去世很久以后，她仍执意住在那里。

usage.note: to 后是被称呼的对象，as 后是名称或身份。
usage.example: She always referred to them as ‘the shifting population’, for they came and went with such frequency that I never even got a chance to learn their names.
usage.exampleZh: 她总称他们为“流动人口”，因为他们来来去去太频繁，我甚至都没有机会记住他们的名字。

usage.note: in charge of 表示负责管理；本例为被动结构，被任命者是 she。
usage.example: During that time she so gained my aunt’s confidence, that she was put in charge of the domestic staff.
usage.exampleZh: 在那段时间里，她深得姨妈信任，以至于被任命为家佣的主管。

usage.note: to 是介词，后接名词或动名词；此处在已有优点上继续补充。
usage.example: In addition to all her other qualifications, Bessie was an expert cook.
usage.exampleZh: 除了其他种种长处，贝茜还是一位烹饪能手。

usage.note: that 后接结论内容；come to 强调形成判断的过程。
usage.example: She reluctantly came to the conclusion that Bessie was drunk.
usage.exampleZh: 她不得不承认一个自己不愿接受的结论：贝茜喝醉了。

rows.en: The New Year is a time for resolutions.
rows.zh: 新年是下决心的时候。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Mentally, at least, most of us could compile formidable lists of ‘dos’ and ‘don’ts’.
rows.zh: 至少在脑海里，我们大多数人都能列出一长串该做和不该做的事，长得令人望而生畏。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The same old favourites recur year in year out with monotonous regularity.
rows.zh: 年复一年，反复出现的总是那些老项目，规律得单调乏味。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We resolve to get up earlier each morning, eat less, find more time to play with the children, do a thousand and one jobs about the house, be nice to people we don’t like, drive carefully, and take the dog for a walk every day.
rows.zh: 我们决心每天早上起得更早，少吃一点，多找时间陪孩子玩，处理家里千头万绪的杂事，对不喜欢的人也友善一些，开车小心，每天遛狗。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Past experience has taught us that certain accomplishments are beyond attainment.
rows.zh: 以往的经验让我们明白，有些目标是办不到的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If we remain inveterate smokers, it is only because we have so often experienced the frustration that results from failure.
rows.zh: 如果我们仍是烟瘾深重的人，那只是因为我们太多次经历了失败带来的挫败感。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Most of us fail in our efforts at self-improvement because our schemes are too ambitious and we never have time to carry them out.
rows.zh: 我们大多数人在自我改进上的努力以失败告终，是因为计划太过宏大，始终没有时间付诸实行。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We also make the fundamental error of announcing our resolutions to everybody so that we look even more foolish when we slip back into our bad old ways.
rows.zh: 我们还犯了一个根本性的错误：逢人便宣布自己的决心，以至于重蹈老习惯时，显得更加可笑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Aware of these pitfalls, this year I attempted to keep my resolutions to myself.
rows.zh: 意识到这些陷阱后，今年我试着把自己的决心藏在心里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I limited myself to two modest ambitions: to do physical exercises every morning and to read more of an evening.
rows.zh: 我只给自己定了两个不算高的目标：每天早上锻炼身体，晚上多读点书。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: An all-night party on New Year’s Eve provided me with a good excuse for not carrying out either of these new resolutions on the first day of the year, but on the second, I applied myself assiduously to the task.
rows.zh: 除夕的一场通宵聚会，让我有了一个很好的借口，新年第一天两项新决心都没实行；但到了第二天，我就勤勤恳恳地投入了行动。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The daily exercises lasted only eleven minutes and I proposed to do them early in the morning before anyone had got up.
rows.zh: 每天的锻炼只需十一分钟，我打算在清早别人都还没起床时做完。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The self-discipline required to drag myself out of bed eleven minutes earlier than usual was considerable.
rows.zh: 要比平常早十一分钟强迫自己离开被窝，需要相当大的自制力。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Nevertheless, I managed to creep down into the living room for two days before anyone found me out.
rows.zh: 尽管如此，我还是悄悄溜到楼下客厅练了两天，才被人发现。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After jumping about on the carpet and twisting the human frame into uncomfortable positions, I sat down at the breakfast table in an exhausted condition.
rows.zh: 在地毯上又蹦又跳，把身体扭成各种不舒服的姿势后，我精疲力竭地坐到早餐桌前。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was this that betrayed me.
rows.zh: 正是这一点泄露了我的秘密。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The next morning the whole family trooped in to watch the performance.
rows.zh: 第二天早上，全家人都成群结队地进来观看表演。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: That was really unsettling, but I fended off the taunts and jibes of the family good-humouredly and soon everybody got used to the idea.
rows.zh: 这实在让我很不自在，不过我好脾气地招架住家人的冷嘲热讽，很快大家也就习以为常了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: However, my enthusiasm waned.
rows.zh: 然而，我的热情渐渐消退。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The time I spent at exercises gradually diminished.
rows.zh: 我花在锻炼上的时间逐步减少。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Little by little the eleven minutes fell to zero.
rows.zh: 那十一分钟一点点缩减，最后变成了零。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: By January 10th, I was back to where I had started from.
rows.zh: 到了一月十日，我又回到了起点。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I argued that if I spent less time exhausting myself at exercises in the morning, I would keep my mind fresh for reading when I got home from work.
rows.zh: 我给自己辩解说，如果早晨少花些时间锻炼、免得累坏自己，下班回家看书时就能保持头脑清醒。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Resisting the hypnotizing effect of television, I sat in my room for a few evenings with my eyes glued to a book.
rows.zh: 有几个晚上，我抵挡着电视的催眠作用，坐在房间里，眼睛紧盯着书本。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One night, however, feeling cold and lonely, I went downstairs and sat in front of the television pretending to read.
rows.zh: 不过，有一天晚上，我觉得又冷又孤单，就下了楼，坐到电视机前，装着看书。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: That proved to be my undoing, for I soon got back to my old bad habit of dozing off in front of the screen.
rows.zh: 这一步最终毁了我的计划，因为我很快又恢复了在屏幕前打瞌睡的老毛病。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I still haven't given up my resolution to do more reading.
rows.zh: 我仍然没有放弃多读书的决心。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In fact, I have just bought a book entitled How to Read a Thousand Words a Minute.
rows.zh: 事实上，我刚买了一本名叫《如何一分钟读一千词》的书。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Perhaps it will solve my problem, but I just haven't had time to read it!
rows.zh: 也许它能解决我的问题，只是我还没抽出时间来读它！
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 固定习语，强调多年反复不变；通常带有重复得令人厌倦的意味。
usage.example: The same old favourites recur year in year out with monotonous regularity.
usage.exampleZh: 年复一年，反复出现的总是那些老项目，规律得单调乏味。

usage.note: 短语动词接代词宾语时，要把代词放在 carry 和 out 之间。
usage.example: Most of us fail in our efforts at self-improvement because our schemes are too ambitious and we never have time to carry them out.
usage.exampleZh: 我们大多数人在自我改进上的努力以失败告终，是因为计划太过宏大，始终没有时间付诸实行。

usage.meaning: 把……藏在心里不告诉别人
usage.note: to oneself 表示只留给自己，这里强调没有向别人宣布。
usage.example: Aware of these pitfalls, this year I attempted to keep my resolutions to myself.
usage.exampleZh: 意识到这些陷阱后，今年我试着把自己的决心藏在心里。

usage.note: 表示渐进变化，常置于句首或句末。
usage.example: Little by little the eleven minutes fell to zero.
usage.exampleZh: 那十一分钟一点点缩减，最后变成了零。

usage.meaning: 打起瞌睡；迷迷糊糊睡去
usage.note: 强调从清醒进入浅睡的过程，常指并非刻意入睡。
usage.example: That proved to be my undoing, for I soon got back to my old bad habit of dozing off in front of the screen.
usage.exampleZh: 这一步最终毁了我的计划，因为我很快又恢复了在屏幕前打瞌睡的老毛病。

usage.note: 后接名词或动名词；这里现在完成时与 still、not 连用，表示至今未放弃。
usage.example: I still haven't given up my resolution to do more reading.
usage.exampleZh: 我仍然没有放弃多读书的决心。

rows.en: Predicting the future is notoriously difficult.
rows.zh: 预测未来之难，是人所共知的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Who could have imagined, in the mid 1970s, for example, that by the end of the 20th century, computers would be as common in people’s homes as TV sets?
rows.zh: 譬如，在二十世纪七十年代中期，谁能想象到，到了二十世纪末，电脑会在家庭中像电视机一样普遍呢？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the 1970s, computers were common enough, but only in big business, government departments, and large organizations.
rows.zh: 二十世纪七十年代，电脑已相当常见，但仅限于大企业、政府部门和大型机构。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: These were the so-called mainframe machines.
rows.zh: 那就是所谓的大型主机。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Mainframe computers were very large indeed, often occupying whole air-conditioned rooms, employing full-time technicians and run on specially-written software.
rows.zh: 大型主机确实非常庞大，常常占据整间空调房，需要专职技术人员照管，并运行专门编写的软件。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though these large machines still exist, many of their functions have been taken over by small powerful personal computers, commonly known as PCs.
rows.zh: 这些大型机器虽然仍然存在，但它们的许多功能已经被小巧而强大的个人电脑接替，个人电脑通常简称为PC。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In 1975, a primitive machine called the Altair, was launched in the USA.
rows.zh: 一九七五年，美国推出了一种叫作“牛郎星”的原始机器。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It can properly be described as the first ‘home computer’ and it pointed the way to the future.
rows.zh: 把它称为第一台“家用电脑”是恰当的，它为未来指明了方向。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This was followed, at the end of the 1970s, by a machine called an Apple.
rows.zh: 随后，二十世纪七十年代末，又出现了一种名叫“苹果”的机器。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the early 1980s, the computer giant, IBM produced the world’s first Personal Computer.
rows.zh: 二十世纪八十年代初，电脑巨头IBM制造了世界上第一台个人电脑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This ran on an ‘operating system’ called DOS, produced by a then small company named Microsoft.
rows.zh: 它使用一种名叫DOS的“操作系统”，由当时一家叫微软的小公司开发。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The IBM Personal Computer was widely copied.
rows.zh: IBM的个人电脑被广泛仿制。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: From those humble beginnings, we have seen the development of the user-friendly home computers and multimedia machines which are in common use today.
rows.zh: 从这些不起眼的开端，我们看到了如今普遍使用、操作便捷的家用电脑和多媒体机器的发展。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Considering how recent these developments are, it is even more remarkable that as long ago as the 1960s, an Englishman, Leon Bagrit, was able to predict some of the uses of computers which we know today.
rows.zh: 考虑到这些发展都是如此近来的事，早在二十世纪六十年代，一位名叫利昂·巴格里特的英国人就能预见到我们今天熟知的电脑的一些用途，便更显得非同寻常。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Bagrit dismissed the idea that computers would learn to ‘think’ for themselves and would ‘rule the world’, which people liked to believe in those days.
rows.zh: 巴格里特不认同当时人们乐于相信的一种说法，即电脑会学会自行“思考”，并且“统治世界”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Bagrit foresaw a time when computers would be small enough to hold in the hand, when they would be capable of providing information about traffic jams and suggesting alternative routes, when they would be used in hospitals to help doctors to diagnose illnesses, when they would relieve office workers and accountants of dull, repetitive clerical work.
rows.zh: 巴格里特预见，有一天电脑会小到可以拿在手里，会提供交通拥堵信息并建议其他路线，会被用于医院协助医生诊断疾病，还会把办公室职员和会计从枯燥、重复的文书工作中解放出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All these computer uses have become commonplace.
rows.zh: 电脑的所有这些用途，都已经变得司空见惯。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Of course, Leon Bagrit could not possibly have foreseen the development of the Internet, the worldwide system that enables us to communicate instantly with anyone in any part of the world by using computers linked to telephone networks.
rows.zh: 当然，利昂·巴格里特绝不可能预见互联网的发展；这个覆盖全球的系统，让我们能借助连接电话网络的电脑，与世界任何地方的任何人即时通信。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Nor could he have foreseen how we could use the Internet to obtain information on every known subject, so we can read it on a screen in our homes and even print it as well if we want to.
rows.zh: 他也不可能预见，我们能够通过互联网获取各个已知领域的信息，在家中的屏幕上阅读，需要时甚至还能打印出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Computers have become smaller and smaller, more and more powerful and cheaper and cheaper.
rows.zh: 电脑变得越来越小、功能越来越强、价格也越来越低。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This is what makes Leon Bagrit’s predictions particularly remarkable.
rows.zh: 这正是利昂·巴格里特的预言格外令人惊叹的原因。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If he, or someone like him, were alive today, he might be able to tell us what to expect in the next fifty years.
rows.zh: 如果他，或像他这样的人，今天还活着，也许能告诉我们未来五十年会有什么事情发生。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 这里以功能作被接替的对象，表示由新的机器承担原来的工作。
usage.example: Though these large machines still exist, many of their functions have been taken over by small powerful personal computers, commonly known as PCs.
usage.exampleZh: 这些大型机器虽然仍然存在，但它们的许多功能已经被小巧而强大的个人电脑接替，个人电脑通常简称为PC。

usage.note: 既可指实际道路，也常比喻为未来发展提供方向。
usage.example: It can properly be described as the first ‘home computer’ and it pointed the way to the future.
usage.exampleZh: 把它称为第一台“家用电脑”是恰当的，它为未来指明了方向。

usage.note: 常与 be 连用，说明某项技术或某种说法已广泛应用。
usage.example: From those humble beginnings, we have seen the development of the user-friendly home computers and multimedia machines which are in common use today.
usage.exampleZh: 从这些不起眼的开端，我们看到了如今普遍使用、操作便捷的家用电脑和多媒体机器的发展。

usage.matchedForm: relieve office workers and accountants of
usage.note: of 后接负担或职责，表示减轻或解除某人承担的工作。
usage.example: Bagrit foresaw a time when computers would be small enough to hold in the hand, when they would be capable of providing information about traffic jams and suggesting alternative routes, when they would be used in hospitals to help doctors to diagnose illnesses, when they would relieve office workers and accountants of dull, repetitive clerical work.
usage.exampleZh: 巴格里特预见，有一天电脑会小到可以拿在手里，会提供交通拥堵信息并建议其他路线，会被用于医院协助医生诊断疾病，还会把办公室职员和会计从枯燥、重复的文书工作中解放出来。

usage.note: commonplace 在这里作形容词，强调原本新奇的事如今十分普遍。
usage.example: All these computer uses have become commonplace.
usage.exampleZh: 电脑的所有这些用途，都已经变得司空见惯。

rows.en: My cousin, Harry, keeps a large curiously-shaped bottle on permanent display in his study.
rows.zh: 我的表兄哈里在书房里一直摆着一只形状古怪的大瓶子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Despite the fact that the bottle is tinted a delicate shade of green, an observant visitor would soon notice that it is filled with what looks like a thick, greyish substance.
rows.zh: 瓶身虽然带着一层淡淡的绿色，细心的来客却很快就会看出，里面装满了某种看上去黏稠、呈灰色的东西。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If you were to ask Harry what was in the bottle, he would tell you that it contained perfumed mud.
rows.zh: 你要是问哈里瓶里装的是什么，他会告诉你，里面是香泥。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If you expressed doubt or surprise, he would immediately invite you to smell it and then to rub some into your skin.
rows.zh: 你要是表示怀疑或惊讶，他会立刻请你闻一闻，再抹一点在皮肤上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This brief experiment would dispel any further doubts you might have.
rows.zh: 这番简短的试验，会让你不再有任何疑问。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The bottle really does contain perfumed mud.
rows.zh: 瓶里确实装着香泥。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: How Harry came into the possession of this outlandish stuff makes an interesting story which he is fond of relating.
rows.zh: 哈里如何得到这种稀奇古怪的东西，是一个有趣的故事，他很爱把它讲给别人听。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Furthermore, the acquisition of this bottle cured him of a bad habit he had been developing for years.
rows.zh: 而且，得到这只瓶子，还治好了他多年来逐渐养成的一个坏习惯。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Harry used to consider it a great joke to go into expensive cosmetic shops and make outrageous requests for goods that do not exist.
rows.zh: 哈里过去常把这样一件事当作大乐子：走进高档化妆品店，提出一些离谱的要求，索要根本不存在的商品。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He would invent fanciful names on the spot.
rows.zh: 他会当场编出各种异想天开的名称。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: On entering a shop, he would ask for a new perfume called ‘Scented Shadow’ or for ‘insoluble bath cubes’.
rows.zh: 一进商店，他就要一种叫“香影”的新香水，或者“不溶解的沐浴块”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If a shop assistant told him she had not heard of it, he would pretend to be considerably put out.
rows.zh: 要是女店员告诉他没听说过，他就装出十分不快的样子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He loved to be told that one of his imaginary products was temporarily out of stock and he would faithfully promise to call again at some future date, but of course he never did.
rows.zh: 他最喜欢听店员说，他虚构的某种产品只是暂时缺货；他还会信誓旦旦地答应改天再来，当然，他从来不来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: How Harry managed to keep a straight face during these performances is quite beyond me.
rows.zh: 哈里表演这些把戏时，怎么能一直板着面孔不笑，我真是无法理解。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Harry does not need to be prompted to explain how he bought his precious bottle of mud.
rows.zh: 用不着别人提醒，哈里就会主动讲起自己怎样买下那瓶珍贵的香泥。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One day, he went to an exclusive shop in London and asked for ‘Myrolite’.
rows.zh: 有一天，他走进伦敦一家高档商店，开口就要“迈罗莱特”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The shop assistant looked puzzled and Harry repeated the word, slowly stressing each syllable.
rows.zh: 女店员露出困惑的神色，哈里又慢慢重复了一遍，把每个音节都念得格外清楚。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When the woman shook her head in bewilderment, Harry went on to explain that ‘myrolite’ was a hard, amber-like substance which could be used to remove freckles.
rows.zh: 那位女士迷惑地摇摇头，哈里便接着解释说，“迈罗莱特”是一种类似琥珀的坚硬物质，可以用来去雀斑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This explanation evidently conveyed something to the woman who searched shelf after shelf.
rows.zh: 这番解释显然让那位女士想到了什么，她开始一架接一架地寻找。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She produced all sorts of weird concoctions, but none of them met with Harry's requirements.
rows.zh: 她拿出各种古怪的调制品，却没有一种符合哈里的要求。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When Harry put on his act of being mildly annoyed, the assistant promised to order some for him.
rows.zh: 哈里装出略微恼火的样子，店员便答应替他订一些。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Intoxicated by his success, Harry then asked for perfumed mud.
rows.zh: 哈里被自己的成功冲昏了头，接着又要香泥。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He expected the assistant to look at him in blank astonishment.
rows.zh: 他本以为店员会满脸茫然、惊愕地看着自己。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: However, it was his turn to be surprised, for the woman’s eyes immediately lit up and she fetched several bottles which she placed on the counter for Harry to inspect.
rows.zh: 然而，这回轮到他吃惊了：那位女士顿时眼睛一亮，取来几只瓶子，放在柜台上让哈里查看。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For once, Harry had to admit defeat.
rows.zh: 这一次，哈里不得不认输了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He picked up what seemed to be the smallest bottle and discreetly asked the price.
rows.zh: 他拿起看来最小的一瓶，小心翼翼地问价钱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He was glad to get away with a mere twenty pounds and he beat a hasty retreat, clutching the precious bottle under his arm.
rows.zh: 只付出二十英镑便能脱身，他已经很高兴了，连忙把那只珍贵的瓶子夹在胳膊下面，匆匆撤退。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: From then on, Harry decided that this little game he had invented might prove to be expensive.
rows.zh: 从那以后，哈里就认定，自己发明的这场小游戏，玩起来可能要花不少钱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The curious bottle, which now adorns the bookcase in his study, was his first and last purchase of rare cosmetics.
rows.zh: 如今点缀在他书房书柜上的这只怪瓶子，是他第一次、也是最后一次购买罕见的化妆品。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: of 后接疾病或坏习惯；这里把坏习惯比作需要治愈的问题。
usage.example: Furthermore, the acquisition of this bottle cured him of a bad habit he had been developing for years.
usage.exampleZh: 而且，得到这只瓶子，还治好了他多年来逐渐养成的一个坏习惯。

usage.note: 这里指无需准备就立即编出，不是只说明地理位置。
usage.example: He would invent fanciful names on the spot.
usage.exampleZh: 他会当场编出各种异想天开的名称。

usage.note: 可与 be 或 temporarily 连用；反义表达为 in stock。
usage.example: He loved to be told that one of his imaginary products was temporarily out of stock and he would faithfully promise to call again at some future date, but of course he never did.
usage.exampleZh: 他最喜欢听店员说，他虚构的某种产品只是暂时缺货；他还会信誓旦旦地答应改天再来，当然，他从来不来。

usage.note: 通常用于明知可笑却努力保持严肃的情景，face 前保留 a。
usage.example: How Harry managed to keep a straight face during these performances is quite beyond me.
usage.exampleZh: 哈里表演这些把戏时，怎么能一直板着面孔不笑，我真是无法理解。

usage.note: defeat 在这个固定搭配中不加冠词，指承认自己失败。
usage.example: For once, Harry had to admit defeat.
usage.exampleZh: 这一次，哈里不得不认输了。

usage.note: 常带诙谐语气，可描述在尴尬场合赶紧离开。
usage.example: He was glad to get away with a mere twenty pounds and he beat a hasty retreat, clutching the precious bottle under his arm.
usage.exampleZh: 只付出二十英镑便能脱身，他已经很高兴了，连忙把那只珍贵的瓶子夹在胳膊下面，匆匆撤退。

rows.en: The Scandinavian countries are much admired all over the world for their enlightened social policies.
rows.zh: 斯堪的纳维亚各国因其开明的社会政策，在全世界广受赞誉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Sweden has evolved an excellent system for protecting the individual citizen from high-handed or incompetent public officers.
rows.zh: 瑞典逐步建立了一套出色的制度，保护公民个人不受专横或不称职的公职人员侵害。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The system has worked so well, that it has been adopted in other countries too.
rows.zh: 这套制度成效甚佳，其他国家也采用了它。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Swedes were the first to recognize that public officials like civil servants, police officers, health inspectors or tax-collectors can make mistakes or act over-zealously in the belief that they are serving the public.
rows.zh: 瑞典人最先认识到，公务员、警察、卫生检查员或税务人员等公职人员，可能会出错，也可能因自以为是在为公众服务而行事过火。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As long ago as 1809, the Swedish Parliament introduced a scheme to safeguard the interest of the individual.
rows.zh: 早在一八〇九年，瑞典议会就推出了一项保护个人利益的制度。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A parliamentary committee representing all political parties appoints a person who is suitably qualified to investigate private grievances against the State.
rows.zh: 一个代表所有政党的议会委员会，会任命一位具备适当资格的人，调查个人针对国家机关提出的申诉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The official title of the person is ‘Justiteombudsman’, but the Swedes commonly refer to him as the ‘J.O.’ or ‘Ombudsman’.
rows.zh: 此人的正式头衔是“Justiteombudsman”，不过瑞典人通常简称他为“J.O.”或“Ombudsman”，即监察专员。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Ombudsman is not subject to political pressure.
rows.zh: 监察专员不受政治压力左右。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He investigates complaints large and small that come to him from all levels of society.
rows.zh: 他调查来自社会各阶层、提交给他的各种大小申诉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As complaints must be made in writing, the Ombudsman receives an average of 1,200 letters a year.
rows.zh: 申诉必须以书面形式提出，因此监察专员平均每年收到一千二百封信。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He has eight lawyer assistants to help him and he examines every single letter in detail.
rows.zh: 他有八位律师助手协助工作，并会详细审阅每一封来信。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There is nothing secretive about the Ombudsman’s work, for his correspondence is open to public inspection.
rows.zh: 监察专员的工作没有什么保密之处，因为他的往来函件都可供公众查阅。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If a citizen’s complaint is justified, the Ombudsman will act on his behalf.
rows.zh: 如果公民的申诉有理，监察专员就会代表他采取行动。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The action he takes varies according to the nature of the complaint.
rows.zh: 他采取什么行动，取决于申诉的性质。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He may gently reprimand an official or even suggest to parliament that a law be altered.
rows.zh: 他可能会温和地训诫某位官员，甚至可能向议会建议修改某项法律。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The following case is a typical example of the Ombudsman's work.
rows.zh: 下面这个案例，就是监察专员工作的一个典型例子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A foreigner living in a Swedish village wrote to the Ombudsman complaining that he had been ill-treated by the police, simply because he was a foreigner.
rows.zh: 一位住在瑞典某村庄的外国人写信给监察专员，投诉自己仅仅因为是外国人，就受到了警察的粗暴对待。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Ombudsman immediately wrote to the Chief of Police in the district asking him to send a record of the case.
rows.zh: 监察专员立刻写信给该地区的警察局长，要求他寄来这个案件的记录。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There was nothing in the record to show that the foreigner’s complaint was justified and the Chief of Police strongly denied the accusation.
rows.zh: 记录中没有任何内容能够表明该外国人的申诉有理，而警察局长也坚决否认这项指控。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was impossible for the Ombudsman to take action, but when he received a similar complaint from another foreigner in the same village, he immediately sent one of his lawyers to investigate the matter.
rows.zh: 监察专员无法采取行动；但当他又接到同一村庄另一名外国人的类似投诉时，就立即派一位律师去调查此事。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The lawyer ascertained that a policeman had indeed dealt roughly with foreigners on several occasions.
rows.zh: 律师查明，一名警察确实曾好几次粗暴对待外国人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The fact that the policeman was prejudiced against foreigners could not be recorded in the official files.
rows.zh: 那个警察对外国人怀有偏见这一事实，不可能记载在官方档案里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was only possible for the Ombudsman to find this out by sending one of his representatives to check the facts.
rows.zh: 监察专员只有派一位代表去核查事实，才能查出这一情况。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The policeman in question was severely reprimanded and was informed that if any further complaints were lodged against him, he would be prosecuted.
rows.zh: 涉事警察受到严厉训斥，并被告知，如果再有人投诉他，他就会受到起诉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Ombudsman’s prompt action at once put an end to an unpleasant practice which might have gone unnoticed.
rows.zh: 监察专员的迅速行动，立刻终止了一种原本可能无人察觉的恶劣做法。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: from 后接威胁来源；强调使保护对象不受到伤害或侵害。
usage.example: Sweden has evolved an excellent system for protecting the individual citizen from high-handed or incompetent public officers.
usage.exampleZh: 瑞典逐步建立了一套出色的制度，保护公民个人不受专横或不称职的公职人员侵害。

usage.note: subject 在这里作形容词，to 是介词；否定形式表示不受其左右。
usage.example: The Ombudsman is not subject to political pressure.
usage.exampleZh: 监察专员不受政治压力左右。

usage.note: 用于正式通知、申请或申诉，区别于口头表达。
usage.example: As complaints must be made in writing, the Ombudsman receives an average of 1,200 letters a year.
usage.exampleZh: 申诉必须以书面形式提出，因此监察专员平均每年收到一千二百封信。

usage.meaning: 代表某人；为某人的利益
usage.note: 所有格随所代表的人变化；也可说 on behalf of someone。
usage.example: If a citizen’s complaint is justified, the Ombudsman will act on his behalf.
usage.exampleZh: 如果公民的申诉有理，监察专员就会代表他采取行动。

usage.note: 位于名词之后，指上文正在谈到的人或物；不一定表示有疑问。
usage.example: The policeman in question was severely reprimanded and was informed that if any further complaints were lodged against him, he would be prosecuted.
usage.exampleZh: 涉事警察受到严厉训斥，并被告知，如果再有人投诉他，他就会受到起诉。

usage.note: to 是介词，后接要停止的行为或情况；end 前有 an。
usage.example: The Ombudsman’s prompt action at once put an end to an unpleasant practice which might have gone unnoticed.
usage.exampleZh: 监察专员的迅速行动，立刻终止了一种原本可能无人察觉的恶劣做法。

rows.en: We have been brought up to fear insects.
rows.zh: 我们从小就被教得害怕昆虫。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We regard them as unnecessary creatures that do more harm than good.
rows.zh: 我们把它们看作多余的生物，认为它们弊大于利。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We continually wage war on them, for they contaminate our food, carry diseases, or devour our crops.
rows.zh: 我们不断向它们开战，因为它们污染食物、传播疾病，或吞食庄稼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They sting or bite without provocation; they fly uninvited into our rooms on summer nights, or beat against our lighted windows.
rows.zh: 它们会无缘无故地蜇人或咬人；夏夜里不请自来地飞进房间，或者撞击亮着灯的窗户。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We live in dread not only of unpleasant insects like spiders or wasps, but of quite harmless ones like moths.
rows.zh: 我们不仅害怕蜘蛛、黄蜂这类讨厌的虫子，甚至也害怕飞蛾这类完全无害的虫子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Reading about them increases our understanding without dispelling our fears.
rows.zh: 阅读有关它们的书，虽能增进了解，却不能消除恐惧。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Knowing that the industrious ant lives in a highly organized society does nothing to prevent us from being filled with revulsion when we find hordes of them crawling over a carefully prepared picnic lunch.
rows.zh: 即使知道勤劳的蚂蚁生活在一个组织严密的社会里，当我们发现成群的蚂蚁爬满精心准备的野餐午饭时，也仍然会满心厌恶。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: No matter how much we like honey, or how much we have read about the uncanny sense of direction which bees possess, we have a horror of being stung.
rows.zh: 无论我们多么喜欢蜂蜜，读过多少关于蜜蜂那神奇方向感的文章，还是会害怕被蜇。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Most of our fears are unreasonable; but they are impossible to erase.
rows.zh: 我们的恐惧大多没有道理，却又无法消除。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At the same time, however, insects are strangely fascinating.
rows.zh: 然而与此同时，昆虫又有一种奇妙的吸引力。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We enjoy reading about them, especially when we find that, like the praying mantis, they lead perfectly horrible lives.
rows.zh: 我们爱读关于它们的故事，尤其当我们发现，它们像螳螂一样，过着极其可怕的生活时。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We enjoy staring at them, entranced as they go about their business, unaware (we hope) of our presence.
rows.zh: 我们喜欢出神地盯着它们，看它们各忙各的，浑然不觉我们在场——但愿如此。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Who has not stood in awe at the sight of a spider pouncing on a fly, or a column of ants triumphantly bearing home an enormous dead beetle?
rows.zh: 看到蜘蛛扑向苍蝇，或一队蚂蚁得意地把一只巨大的死甲虫抬回家，谁不曾肃然惊叹？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Last summer I spent days in the garden watching thousands of ants crawling up the trunk of my prize peach tree.
rows.zh: 去年夏天，我在花园里接连几天观察成千上万只蚂蚁，看它们沿着我那棵引以为傲的桃树的树干往上爬。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The tree has grown against a warm wall on a sheltered side of the house.
rows.zh: 这棵树靠着房屋背风一侧的一面温暖的墙生长。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I am especially proud of it, not only because it has survived several severe winters, but because it occasionally produces luscious peaches.
rows.zh: 我对它格外自豪，不仅因为它熬过了几个严冬，还因为它偶尔能结出甘美多汁的桃子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: During the summer, I noticed that the leaves of the tree were beginning to wither.
rows.zh: 夏天里，我注意到树叶开始枯萎。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Clusters of tiny insects called aphids were to be found on the underside of the leaves.
rows.zh: 叶子的背面能看到一团团叫作蚜虫的小虫。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They were visited by a large colony of ants which obtained a sort of honey from them.
rows.zh: 一大群蚂蚁经常来找它们，从它们身上取得一种蜜汁。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I immediately embarked on an experiment which, even though it failed to get rid of the ants, kept me fascinated for twenty-four hours.
rows.zh: 我立刻着手做了一项试验；虽然没能赶走蚂蚁，却让我整整二十四小时着迷不已。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I bound the base of the tree with sticky tape, making it impossible for the ants to reach the aphids.
rows.zh: 我用黏胶带缠住树干基部，让蚂蚁无法接近蚜虫。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The tape was so sticky that they did not dare to cross it.
rows.zh: 胶带黏得厉害，蚂蚁不敢从上面爬过去。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For a long time, I watched them scurrying around the base of the tree in bewilderment.
rows.zh: 我久久地看着它们困惑地在树根周围匆匆乱跑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I even went out at midnight with a torch and noted with satisfaction (and surprise) that the ants were still swarming around the sticky tape without being able to do anything about it.
rows.zh: 我甚至在半夜拿着手电筒出去，满意又惊讶地发现，蚂蚁仍在黏胶带周围聚作一团，束手无策。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I got up early next morning hoping to find that the ants had given up in despair.
rows.zh: 第二天一早我就起了床，希望看到蚂蚁已经绝望地放弃。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Instead, I saw that they had discovered a new route.
rows.zh: 但我看到的却是，它们已经找到了一条新路线。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They were climbing up the wall of the house and then on to the leaves of the tree.
rows.zh: 它们先爬上房子的墙，再爬到树叶上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I realized sadly that I had been completely defeated by their ingenuity.
rows.zh: 我沮丧地意识到，自己已经彻底败给了它们的机灵。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The ants had been quick to find an answer to my thoroughly unscientific methods!
rows.zh: 对于我那完全不科学的办法，蚂蚁很快就找到了对策！
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 这里为被动形式，bring someone up to do something 表示从小培养某种态度或习惯。
usage.example: We have been brought up to fear insects.
usage.exampleZh: 我们从小就被教得害怕昆虫。

usage.note: 固定比较表达，harm 和 good 都作名词，表示坏处和好处。
usage.example: We regard them as unnecessary creatures that do more harm than good.
usage.exampleZh: 我们把它们看作多余的生物，认为它们弊大于利。

usage.note: 可用于实际战争，也常比喻持续对抗害虫、疾病等问题。
usage.example: We continually wage war on them, for they contaminate our food, carry diseases, or devour our crops.
usage.exampleZh: 我们不断向它们开战，因为它们污染食物、传播疾病，或吞食庄稼。

usage.note: 后接不想保留的人、物或问题；这里指赶走蚂蚁。
usage.example: I immediately embarked on an experiment which, even though it failed to get rid of the ants, kept me fascinated for twenty-four hours.
usage.exampleZh: 我立刻着手做了一项试验；虽然没能赶走蚂蚁，却让我整整二十四小时着迷不已。

usage.note: give up 可单独使用，in despair 补充放弃时的心情。
usage.example: I got up early next morning hoping to find that the ants had given up in despair.
usage.exampleZh: 第二天一早我就起了床，希望看到蚂蚁已经绝望地放弃。

rows.en: Recent developments in astronomy have made it possible to detect planets in our own Milky Way and in other galaxies.
rows.zh: 天文学近期的发展，使人类能够探测到我们银河系以及其他星系中的行星。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This is a major achievement because, in relative terms, planets are very small and do not emit light.
rows.zh: 这是一项重大成就，因为相对而言，行星十分微小，而且自身不发光。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Finding planets is proving hard enough, but finding life on them will prove infinitely more difficult.
rows.zh: 寻找行星已经证明够困难了，但要在行星上寻找生命，难度将大得不可比拟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The first question to answer is whether a planet can actually support life.
rows.zh: 首先需要回答的问题是，一颗行星究竟能不能维持生命。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In our own solar system, for example, Venus is far too hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.
rows.zh: 例如，在我们的太阳系里，金星太热，火星又太冷，都无法维持生命。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Only the Earth provides ideal conditions, and even here it has taken more than four billion years for plant and animal life to evolve.
rows.zh: 只有地球提供了理想的条件；可即便在这里，动植物生命的演化也花了四十多亿年。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Whether a planet can support life depends on the size and brightness of its star, that is its ‘sun’.
rows.zh: 一颗行星能否维持生命，取决于它所属恒星，也就是它的“太阳”的大小和亮度。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Imagine a star up to twenty times larger, brighter and hotter than our own sun.
rows.zh: 想象一颗恒星，它的大小、亮度和温度，都可达到我们太阳的二十倍。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A planet would have to be a very long way from it to be capable of supporting life.
rows.zh: 一颗行星必须离它非常远，才有可能维持生命。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Alternatively, if the star were small, the life-supporting planet would have to have a close orbit round it and also provide the perfect conditions for life forms to develop.
rows.zh: 反过来，如果恒星很小，能够维持生命的行星就必须沿着离它很近的轨道运行，同时还得具备让生命形态发展的完美条件。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But how would we find such a planet?
rows.zh: 可是，我们怎样才能找到这样的行星呢？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At present, there is no telescope in existence that is capable of detecting the presence of life.
rows.zh: 目前，还没有一架现存的望远镜能够探测生命的存在。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The development of such a telescope will be one of the great astronomical projects of the twenty-first century.
rows.zh: 研制这样的望远镜，将成为二十一世纪天文学的重大项目之一。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is impossible to look for life on another planet using earth-based telescopes.
rows.zh: 用设在地球上的望远镜，不可能寻找其他行星上的生命。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Our own warm atmosphere and the heat generated by the telescope would make it impossible to detect objects as small as planets.
rows.zh: 我们自身温暖的大气，以及望远镜产生的热量，会让探测像行星这样小的物体成为不可能。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even a telescope in orbit round the earth, like the very successful Hubble telescope, would not be suitable because of the dust particles in our solar system.
rows.zh: 即使是像极为成功的哈勃望远镜那样绕地球运行的望远镜，也会由于太阳系内的尘埃颗粒而不适合这项任务。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A telescope would have to be as far away as the planet Jupiter to look for life in outer space, because the dust becomes thinner the further we travel towards the outer edges of our own solar system.
rows.zh: 要寻找外太空的生命，望远镜必须远到木星所在的位置，因为越往太阳系外围走，尘埃就越稀薄。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Once we detected a planet, we would have to find a way of blotting out the light from its star, so that we would be able to ‘see’ the planet properly and analyse its atmosphere.
rows.zh: 一旦探测到一颗行星，我们还必须想办法遮住它所属恒星的光，才能真正“看清”这颗行星，分析它的大气。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the first instance, we would be looking for plant life, rather than ‘little green men’.
rows.zh: 最初，我们要寻找的会是植物生命，而不是“小绿人”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The life forms most likely to develop on a planet would be bacteria.
rows.zh: 一颗行星上最可能发展出的生命形态，会是细菌。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.
rows.zh: 正是细菌产生了我们在地球上呼吸的氧气。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For most of the earth’s history they have been the only form of life on our planet.
rows.zh: 在地球历史的大部分时期，它们都是这个星球上唯一的生命形态。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As Earth-dwellers, we always cherish the hope that we will be visited by little green men and that we will be able to communicate with them.
rows.zh: 身为地球居民，我们总怀着希望，盼着小绿人来访，并且能够与他们沟通。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But this hope is always in the realms of science fiction.
rows.zh: 不过，这种希望始终只存在于科幻领域之中。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If we were able to discover lowly forms of life like bacteria on another planet, it would completely change our view of ourselves.
rows.zh: 如果我们能在另一颗行星上发现像细菌这样的低等生命，就会彻底改变我们对自身的看法。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As Daniel Goldin of NASA observed, ‘Finding life elsewhere would change everything.
rows.zh: 正如美国国家航空航天局的丹尼尔·戈尔丁所说：“在别处发现生命，将会改变一切。
rows.speaker: 丹尼尔·戈尔丁

rows.en: No human endeavour or thought would be unchanged by it.’
rows.zh: 人类的任何努力、任何思想，都会因此发生改变。”
rows.speaker: 丹尼尔·戈尔丁

usage.note: 用于说明判断是比较后的结果，避免把相对大小说成绝对大小。
usage.example: This is a major achievement because, in relative terms, planets are very small and do not emit light.
usage.exampleZh: 这是一项重大成就，因为相对而言，行星十分微小，而且自身不发光。

usage.note: support 在此指提供生存条件，不是对某种看法表示支持。
usage.example: The first question to answer is whether a planet can actually support life.
usage.exampleZh: 首先需要回答的问题是，一颗行星究竟能不能维持生命。

usage.note: 常用于遮住光线或视线，也可引申为从记忆中抹去。
usage.example: Once we detected a planet, we would have to find a way of blotting out the light from its star, so that we would be able to ‘see’ the planet properly and analyse its atmosphere.
usage.exampleZh: 一旦探测到一颗行星，我们还必须想办法遮住它所属恒星的光，才能真正“看清”这颗行星，分析它的大气。

usage.note: 强调行动或考虑的第一步，常用于较正式的表达。
usage.example: In the first instance, we would be looking for plant life, rather than ‘little green men’.
usage.exampleZh: 最初，我们要寻找的会是植物生命，而不是“小绿人”。

usage.note: that 后接希望实现的事情；cherish 带有珍视并长期抱有的意味。
usage.example: As Earth-dwellers, we always cherish the hope that we will be visited by little green men and that we will be able to communicate with them.
usage.exampleZh: 身为地球居民，我们总怀着希望，盼着小绿人来访，并且能够与他们沟通。

rows.en: The river which forms the eastern boundary of our farm has always played an important part in our lives.
rows.zh: 那条构成我们农场东部边界的河，一直在我们的生活中扮演着重要角色。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Without it we could not make a living.
rows.zh: 没有它，我们就无法谋生。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There is only enough spring water to supply the needs of the house, so we have to pump from the river for farm use.
rows.zh: 泉水只够供家里生活所需，所以农场用水必须从河里抽取。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We tell the river all our secrets.
rows.zh: 我们把所有秘密都告诉这条河。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We know instinctively, just as beekeepers with their bees, that misfortune might overtake us if the important events of our lives were not related to it.
rows.zh: 正如养蜂人与蜜蜂之间的关系一样，我们本能地知道，如果不把生活中的重大事情讲给河听，厄运就可能降临到我们头上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We have special river birthday parties in the summer.
rows.zh: 夏天，我们会举办别具一格的河畔生日聚会。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Sometimes we go upstream to a favourite backwater, sometimes we have our party at the boathouse, which a predecessor of ours at the farm built in the meadow hard by the deepest pool for swimming and diving.
rows.zh: 有时，我们逆流而上，去一处最喜欢的回水湾；有时就在船屋聚会，那是以前经营这座农场的一位主人，建在紧挨着最深水潭的草地上的，供游泳和跳水之用。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In a heat wave we choose a midnight birthday party and that is the most exciting of all.
rows.zh: 热浪来袭时，我们选择在午夜开生日聚会，这种聚会是最令人兴奋的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We welcome the seasons by the riverside, crowning the youngest girl with flowers in the spring, holding a summer festival on Midsummer Eve, giving thanks for the harvest in the autumn, and throwing a holly wreath into the current in the winter.
rows.zh: 我们在河边迎接四季：春天给最小的女孩戴上花冠，仲夏前夜举行夏日庆典，秋天感谢丰收，冬天则把冬青花环投入水流。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After a long period of rain the river may overflow its banks.
rows.zh: 久雨之后，河水可能漫过两岸。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This is a rare occurrence as our climate seldom goes to extremes.
rows.zh: 这种情况很少发生，因为我们这里的气候很少走向极端。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We are lucky in that only the lower fields, which make up a very small proportion of our farm, are affected by flooding, but other farms are less favourably sited, and flooding can sometimes spell disaster for their owners.
rows.zh: 我们很幸运，只有低洼的田地会受洪水影响，而这些田地只占农场很小的一部分；但别的农场位置没这么好，洪水有时会给农场主带来灾难。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One bad winter we watched the river creep up the lower meadows.
rows.zh: 有一年冬天格外恶劣，我们看着河水慢慢漫上地势较低的草场。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All the cattle had been moved into stalls and we stood to lose little.
rows.zh: 牛群已全都赶进牛棚，因此我们预计损失不会很大。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We were, however, worried about our nearest neighbours, whose farm was low lying and who were newcomers to the district.
rows.zh: 不过，我们担心最近的邻居；他们的农场地势低，而且他们刚搬来这个地区不久。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As the floods had put the telephone out of order, we could not find out how they were managing.
rows.zh: 洪水使电话出了故障，我们无法打听他们应付得怎么样。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: From an attic window we could get a sweeping view of the river where their land joined ours, and at the most critical juncture we took turns in watching that point.
rows.zh: 从阁楼的窗户望去，我们能把两家土地相接处的河段尽收眼底；到了最危急的关头，我们轮流守望着那里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The first sign of disaster was a dead sheep floating down.
rows.zh: 灾难最初的迹象，是一只顺流漂下来的死羊。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Next came a horse, swimming bravely, but we were afraid that the strength of the current would prevent its landing anywhere before it became exhausted.
rows.zh: 接着来了一匹马，奋力游着；但我们担心，水流太强，它恐怕还来不及找到地方上岸，就会筋疲力尽。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Suddenly a raft appeared, looking rather like Noah's ark, carrying the whole family, a few hens, the dogs, a cat, and a bird in a cage.
rows.zh: 突然，一只木筏出现了，看起来颇像诺亚方舟，上面载着那一家人、几只母鸡、几条狗、一只猫，还有笼中的一只鸟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We realized that they must have become unduly frightened by the rising flood, for their house, which had sound foundations, would have stood stoutly even if it had been almost submerged.
rows.zh: 我们明白，他们一定是被不断上涨的洪水吓过了头，因为他们的房子地基牢固，即使几乎被水淹没，也会坚稳地屹立着。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The men of our family waded down through our flooded meadows with boathooks, in the hope of being able to grapple a corner of the raft and pull it out of the current towards our bank.
rows.zh: 我们家的男人拿着船钩，涉过被淹的草场，希望能钩住木筏的一角，把它从急流中拉向我们这边的河岸。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We still think it a miracle that they were able to do so.
rows.zh: 他们居然做到了，我们至今仍觉得这是个奇迹。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: part 在这里指作用或角色；可把 important 换成 major、vital 等。
usage.example: The river which forms the eastern boundary of our farm has always played an important part in our lives.
usage.exampleZh: 那条构成我们农场东部边界的河，一直在我们的生活中扮演着重要角色。

usage.note: 常用 by doing something 说明谋生方式；living 前保留 a。
usage.example: Without it we could not make a living.
usage.exampleZh: 没有它，我们就无法谋生。

usage.note: 可形容人的行为，也可像本例一样形容气候变化过于极端。
usage.example: This is a rare occurrence as our climate seldom goes to extremes.
usage.exampleZh: 这种情况很少发生，因为我们这里的气候很少走向极端。

usage.meaning: 发生故障；不能正常使用
usage.note: 常用于电话、机器等设备；在别的语境中也可指秩序不当。
usage.example: As the floods had put the telephone out of order, we could not find out how they were managing.
usage.exampleZh: 洪水使电话出了故障，我们无法打听他们应付得怎么样。

usage.note: 表示几个人交替承担同一件事；也常用 take turns doing。
usage.example: From an attic window we could get a sweeping view of the river where their land joined ours, and at the most critical juncture we took turns in watching that point.
usage.exampleZh: 从阁楼的窗户望去，我们能把两家土地相接处的河段尽收眼底；到了最危急的关头，我们轮流守望着那里。

usage.note: of 后接名词或动名词；若用 that，则后接完整句子。
usage.example: The men of our family waded down through our flooded meadows with boathooks, in the hope of being able to grapple a corner of the raft and pull it out of the current towards our bank.
usage.exampleZh: 我们家的男人拿着船钩，涉过被淹的草场，希望能钩住木筏的一角，把它从急流中拉向我们这边的河岸。

rows.en: I stopped to let the car cool off and to study the map.
rows.zh: 我停下车，让汽车降降温，也研究一下地图。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I had expected to be near my objective by now, but everything still seemed alien to me.
rows.zh: 我原以为到这时应该已经接近目的地，可周围一切对我来说仍显得陌生。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I was only five when my father had taken me abroad, and that was eighteen years ago.
rows.zh: 父亲带我出国时，我才五岁，那是十八年前的事了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When my mother had died after a tragic accident, he did not quickly recover from the shock and loneliness.
rows.zh: 母亲在一次悲惨的事故后去世，父亲久久无法从打击和孤独中恢复过来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Everything around him was full of her presence, continually reopening the wound.
rows.zh: 身边处处都留着母亲的影子，不断揭开他心头的伤口。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: So he decided to emigrate.
rows.zh: 于是，他决定移民。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the new country he became absorbed in making a new life for the two of us, so that he gradually ceased to grieve.
rows.zh: 到了新的国家，他一心为我们俩开创新生活，渐渐不再那么悲痛。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He did not marry again and I was brought up without a woman’s care; but I lacked for nothing, for he was both father and mother to me.
rows.zh: 他没有再婚，我在没有女性照料的环境下长大；但我什么也不缺，因为他对我既当父亲，又当母亲。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He always meant to go back one day, but not to stay.
rows.zh: 他一直打算总有一天回去一趟，但并不准备留下来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: His roots and mine had become too firmly embedded in the new land.
rows.zh: 他和我的根，已经在新的土地上扎得太深。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But he wanted to see the old folk again and to visit my mother’s grave.
rows.zh: 不过，他想再看看故乡的父老，也想去母亲墓前祭扫。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He became mortally ill a few months before we had planned to go and, when he knew that he was dying, he made me promise to go on my own.
rows.zh: 在我们计划动身前的几个月，他患上了绝症；知道自己不久于人世时，他要我答应独自回去。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I hired a car the day after landing and bought a comprehensive book of maps, which I found most helpful on the cross-country journey, but which I did not think I should need on the last stage.
rows.zh: 抵达的第二天，我租了一辆汽车，买了一本详尽的地图册；它在横穿乡间的旅程中帮了我很大的忙，但我原以为，最后一段路就用不上它了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was not that I actually remembered anything at all.
rows.zh: 这并不是因为我实际上还记得什么。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But my father had described over and over again what we should see at every milestone, after leaving the nearest town, so that I was positive I should recognize it as familiar territory.
rows.zh: 而是父亲一遍又一遍描述过，离开最近的小镇后，每经过一个里程碑，我们会看到什么，因此我确信自己会认出那片熟悉的地方。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Well, I had been wrong, for I was now lost.
rows.zh: 可是我想错了，因为我现在迷路了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I looked at the map and then at the milometer.
rows.zh: 我看了看地图，又看了看里程表。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I had come ten miles since leaving the town, and at this point, according to my father, I should be looking at farms and cottages in a valley, with the spire of the church of our village showing in the far distance.
rows.zh: 离开小镇以来，我已开了十英里；照父亲的说法，在这里我应该能看到山谷中的农场和村舍，以及远处我们村教堂的尖塔。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I could see no valley, no farms, no cottages and no church spire — only a lake.
rows.zh: 我看不见山谷、农场、村舍，也看不见教堂尖塔——只有一片湖。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I decided that I must have taken a wrong turning somewhere.
rows.zh: 我认定自己一定是在某个地方拐错了路。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: So I drove back to the town and began to retrace the route, taking frequent glances at the map.
rows.zh: 于是我开回小镇，重新沿着那条路线走，不时看一眼地图。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I landed up at the same corner.
rows.zh: 结果，我又回到了同一个转角。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The curious thing was that the lake was not marked on the map.
rows.zh: 奇怪的是，地图上并没有标出这个湖。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I felt as if I had stumbled into a nightmare country, as you sometimes do in dreams.
rows.zh: 我觉得自己好像误入了一个噩梦般的国度，就像有时在梦中会发生的那样。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And, as in a nightmare, there was nobody in sight to help me.
rows.zh: 也像噩梦里一样，视线中没有一个能帮我的人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Fortunately for me, as I was wondering what to do next, there appeared on the horizon a man on horseback, riding in my direction.
rows.zh: 幸好，就在我盘算下一步该怎么办时，地平线上出现了一个骑马的人，正朝我这边过来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I waited till he came near, then I asked him the way to our old village.
rows.zh: 我等他走近，便向他打听通往我们旧日村庄的路。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He said that there was now no village.
rows.zh: 他说，如今已经没有那个村子了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I thought he must have misunderstood me, so I repeated its name.
rows.zh: 我以为他一定误解了我的话，于是又说了一遍村名。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This time he pointed to the lake.
rows.zh: 这一次，他指向了湖。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The village no longer existed because it had been submerged, and all the valley too.
rows.zh: 村庄已经不复存在，因为它连同整个山谷都被水淹没了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The lake was not a natural one, but a man-made reservoir.
rows.zh: 那个湖并不是天然湖泊，而是一座人工水库。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 此处指汽车散热，也可比喻人冷静下来、怒气消退。
usage.example: I stopped to let the car cool off and to study the map.
usage.exampleZh: 我停下车，让汽车降降温，也研究一下地图。

usage.note: in 后接名词或动名词，强调注意力完全投入其中。
usage.example: In the new country he became absorbed in making a new life for the two of us, so that he gradually ceased to grieve.
usage.exampleZh: 到了新的国家，他一心为我们俩开创新生活，渐渐不再那么悲痛。

usage.note: lack for 通常用于否定句；本例强调生活所需得到充分满足。
usage.example: He did not marry again and I was brought up without a woman’s care; but I lacked for nothing, for he was both father and mother to me.
usage.exampleZh: 他没有再婚，我在没有女性照料的环境下长大；但我什么也不缺，因为他对我既当父亲，又当母亲。

usage.note: 强调重复很多次，常用于讲述、练习或检查。
usage.example: But my father had described over and over again what we should see at every milestone, after leaving the nearest town, so that I was positive I should recognize it as familiar territory.
usage.exampleZh: 而是父亲一遍又一遍描述过，离开最近的小镇后，每经过一个里程碑，我们会看到什么，因此我确信自己会认出那片熟悉的地方。

usage.note: 口语中常表示非预期地到达某处，也可用 land up in 或 at 引出地点。
usage.example: I landed up at the same corner.
usage.exampleZh: 结果，我又回到了同一个转角。

rows.en: The old lady was glad to be back at the block of flats where she lived.
rows.zh: 老太太回到自己住的那幢公寓楼，很是高兴。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Her shopping had tired her and her basket had grown heavier with every step of the way home.
rows.zh: 买东西让她累坏了，回家的一路上，每走一步都觉得篮子更重些。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the lift her thoughts were on lunch and a good rest; but when she got out at her own floor, both were forgotten in her sudden discovery that her front door was open.
rows.zh: 坐电梯时，她想着吃午饭、好好休息；可到了自己的楼层一出电梯，突然发现家门开着，这两个念头顿时全忘了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She was thinking that she must reprimand her home help the next morning for such a monstrous piece of negligence, when she remembered that she had gone shopping after the home help had left and she knew that she had turned both keys in their locks.
rows.zh: 她正想着第二天早上一定要责备家务帮工，怎么会如此严重地疏忽，忽然又想起来，自己是在帮工走后才出门购物的，而且她清楚记得，两把钥匙都已在锁里转过、把门锁好了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She walked slowly into the hall and at once noticed that all the room doors were open, yet following her regular practice she had shut them before going out.
rows.zh: 她慢慢走进门厅，马上发现各个房间的门都敞着，可她出门前明明照老习惯把它们都关上了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Looking into the drawing room, she saw a scene of confusion over by her writing desk.
rows.zh: 朝客厅里望去，她看到写字台那边一片狼藉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was as clear as daylight then that burglars had forced an entry during her absence.
rows.zh: 这下再清楚不过了：她不在家时，有窃贼闯了进来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Her first impulse was to go round all the rooms looking for the thieves, but then she decided that at her age it might be more prudent to have someone with her, so she went to fetch the porter from his basement.
rows.zh: 她的第一个念头是挨个房间找一找小偷，但转念又觉得，以自己这把年纪，有个人陪着也许更稳妥，于是便去地下室找门房。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: By this time her legs were beginning to tremble, so she sat down and accepted a cup of very strong tea, while he telephoned the police.
rows.zh: 这时她的双腿开始发抖，便坐下来，接过一杯很浓的茶喝着，而门房则打电话报警。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Then, her composure regained, she was ready to set off with the porter’s assistance to search for any intruders who might still be lurking in her flat.
rows.zh: 随后，她恢复了镇定，准备在门房的协助下出发，搜查可能仍潜伏在公寓里的入侵者。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They went through the rooms, being careful to touch nothing, as they did not want to hinder the police in their search for fingerprints.
rows.zh: 他们逐个房间查看，小心地不碰任何东西，以免妨碍警察寻找指纹。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The chaos was inconceivable.
rows.zh: 屋内的混乱简直难以想象。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She had lived in the flat for thirty years and was a veritable magpie at hoarding; and it seemed as though everything she possessed had been tossed out and turned over and over.
rows.zh: 她在这套公寓里住了三十年，收藏杂物的本领真像一只喜鹊；她所有的东西似乎都被抛了出来，翻了个底朝天。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At least sorting out the things she should have discarded years ago was now being made easier for her.
rows.zh: 至少，那些她多年前就该扔掉的东西，现在更方便清理了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Then a police inspector arrived with a constable and she told them of her discovery of the ransacked flat.
rows.zh: 接着，一位警官带着一名警员赶到，她向他们讲述了自己如何发现家里被洗劫。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The inspector began to look for fingerprints, while the constable checked that the front door locks had not been forced, thereby proving that the burglars had either used skeleton keys or entered over the balcony.
rows.zh: 警官开始寻找指纹，警员则检查并确认前门的锁并未被撬坏，从而证明窃贼要么用了万能钥匙，要么是翻过阳台进来的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There was no trace of fingerprints, but the inspector found a dirty red bundle that contained jewellery which the old lady said was not hers.
rows.zh: 没有找到任何指纹，但警官发现了一个脏兮兮的红色包袱，里面装着首饰，老太太说那不是她的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: So their entry into this flat was apparently not the burglars’ first job that day and they must have been disturbed.
rows.zh: 因此，闯进这套公寓显然不是窃贼当天干的第一起案子，而且他们准是受了惊扰才离开的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The inspector then asked the old lady to try to check what was missing by the next day and advised her not to stay alone in the flat for a few nights.
rows.zh: 警官随后请老太太尽量到第二天时查清丢了什么，并劝她这几晚别独自住在公寓里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The old lady thought he was a fussy creature, but since the porter agreed with him, she rang up her daughter and asked for her help in what she described as a little spot of bother.
rows.zh: 老太太觉得他未免大惊小怪，但既然门房也赞同他的话，她就打电话给女儿，请女儿来帮忙，处理她口中这点“小小的麻烦”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 比喻事实非常明显，常作表语；不要按字面理解为房间很明亮。
usage.example: It was as clear as daylight then that burglars had forced an entry during her absence.
usage.exampleZh: 这下再清楚不过了：她不在家时，有窃贼闯了进来。

usage.note: 此处指开始行动或行程；后面可接 for 引出目的地。
usage.example: Then, her composure regained, she was ready to set off with the porter’s assistance to search for any intruders who might still be lurking in her flat.
usage.exampleZh: 随后，她恢复了镇定，准备在门房的协助下出发，搜查可能仍潜伏在公寓里的入侵者。

usage.note: 表示把杂乱物品分清并妥善处理，也可用于解决问题。
usage.example: At least sorting out the things she should have discarded years ago was now being made easier for her.
usage.exampleZh: 至少，那些她多年前就该扔掉的东西，现在更方便清理了。

usage.note: trace 在这里表示可供发现或追踪的迹象，of 后接所寻找的东西。
usage.example: There was no trace of fingerprints, but the inspector found a dirty red bundle that contained jewellery which the old lady said was not hers.
usage.exampleZh: 没有找到任何指纹，但警官发现了一个脏兮兮的红色包袱，里面装着首饰，老太太说那不是她的。

usage.note: 英式口语中的轻描淡写说法；此处与严重入室盗窃形成幽默反差。
usage.example: The old lady thought he was a fussy creature, but since the porter agreed with him, she rang up her daughter and asked for her help in what she described as a little spot of bother.
usage.exampleZh: 老太太觉得他未免大惊小怪，但既然门房也赞同他的话，她就打电话给女儿，请女儿来帮忙，处理她口中这点“小小的麻烦”。

rows.en: People tend to amass possessions, sometimes without being aware of doing so.
rows.zh: 人们总容易积攒东西，有时自己还浑然不觉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Indeed they can have a delightful surprise when they find something useful which they did not know they owned.
rows.zh: 的确，发现一件原本不知道自己拥有、又派得上用场的东西，会让人惊喜不已。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Those who never have to move house become indiscriminate collectors of what can only be described as clutter.
rows.zh: 那些从不用搬家的人，会不加选择地收藏各种东西，而这些东西只能称作杂物。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They leave unwanted objects in drawers, cupboards and attics for years, in the belief that they may one day need just those very things.
rows.zh: 他们把用不着的物件放在抽屉、橱柜和阁楼里，一放就是多年，坚信自己也许哪天偏偏就会用到它们。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As they grow old, people also accumulate belongings for two other reasons, lack of physical and mental energy, both of which are essential in turning out and throwing away, and sentiment.
rows.zh: 随着年纪增长，人们还会出于另外两个原因积存物品：一是缺乏清理和丢弃东西所必需的体力与精力，二是念旧。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Things owned for a long time are full of associations with the past, perhaps with relatives who are dead, and so they gradually acquire a value beyond their true worth.
rows.zh: 拥有已久的东西，会让人联想起许多往事，也许还会让人想起已故的亲人，因此它们渐渐获得了超出实际价值的意义。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Some things are collected deliberately in the home in an attempt to avoid waste.
rows.zh: 有些东西是人们为避免浪费而有意收存在家里的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Among these I would list string and brown paper, kept by thrifty people when a parcel has been opened, to save buying these two requisites.
rows.zh: 其中我会列入绳子和牛皮纸，节俭的人拆开包裹后会把它们留下，省得再花钱买这两样必需品。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Collecting small items can easily become a mania.
rows.zh: 收集小东西，很容易变成一种癖好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I know someone who always cuts sketches out from newspapers of model clothes that she would like to buy if she had the money.
rows.zh: 我认识一个人，总从报纸上剪下时装样图，那些都是她如果有钱就想买的衣服。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As she is not rich, the chances that she will ever be able to afford such purchases are remote; but she is never sufficiently strong-minded to be able to stop the practice.
rows.zh: 她并不富裕，因此将来真能买得起这些衣服的希望很渺茫；可她又始终缺乏足够的意志力，无法停止这种做法。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is a harmless habit, but it litters up her desk to such an extent that every time she opens it, loose bits of paper fall out in every direction.
rows.zh: 这习惯本身并无害处，却把她的书桌堆得如此杂乱，以至于每次打开抽屉，散碎的纸片都会四处掉出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Collecting as a serious hobby is quite different and has many advantages.
rows.zh: 把收藏当作一种认真的业余爱好，则完全是另一回事，而且好处很多。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It provides relaxation for leisure hours, as just looking at one’s treasures is always a joy.
rows.zh: 它让人能在闲暇时放松，因为光是看看自己的宝贝，就总能令人愉快。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One does not have to go outside for amusement, since the collection is housed at home.
rows.zh: 藏品就存放在家中，所以用不着外出找乐趣。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Whatever it consists of, stamps, records, first editions of books, china, glass, antique furniture, pictures, model cars, stuffed birds, toy animals, there is always something to do in connection with it, from finding the right place for the latest addition, to verifying facts in reference books.
rows.zh: 无论收藏的是什么——邮票、唱片、初版书、瓷器、玻璃器皿、古董家具、画作、模型汽车、鸟类标本，还是玩具动物——总有相关的事情可做，从给新添的藏品寻找合适的位置，到查阅参考书核实资料，都是如此。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This hobby educates one not only in the chosen subject, but also in general matters which have some bearing on it.
rows.zh: 这种爱好不仅让人在选定的领域增长知识，也让人了解与之有关的一般知识。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There are also other benefits.
rows.zh: 此外，还有别的好处。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One wants to meet like-minded collectors, to get advice, to compare notes, to exchange articles, to show off the latest find.
rows.zh: 人们会想结识志趣相投的收藏者，向他们请教、交流心得、交换藏品，并炫耀最新的发现。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: So one’s circle of friends grows.
rows.zh: 于是，朋友圈也就扩大了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Soon the hobby leads to travel, perhaps to a meeting in another town, possibly a trip abroad in search of a rare specimen, for collectors are not confined to any one country.
rows.zh: 不久，这种爱好还会带来旅行：也许是去另一个城镇参加聚会，也许是出国寻觅一件稀有藏品，因为收藏者并不局限于某一个国家。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Over the years, one may well become an authority on one’s hobby and will very probably be asked to give informal talks to little gatherings and then, if successful, to larger audiences.
rows.zh: 多年下来，人们很可能成为自己收藏领域的权威，并很有可能受邀在小型聚会上作非正式的讲述；讲得好，还会面对更多听众。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In this way self-confidence grows, first from mastering a subject, then from being able to talk about it.
rows.zh: 这样，自信心逐渐增长，先是来自掌握了一个领域的知识，再是来自能够把这些知识讲出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Collecting, by occupying spare time so constructively, makes a person contented, with no time for boredom.
rows.zh: 收藏让人如此有益地利用闲暇，带来满足，也让人没有时间感到无聊。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: of 是介词，后接名词或动名词；也可用 be aware that 引出完整句子。
usage.example: People tend to amass possessions, sometimes without being aware of doing so.
usage.exampleZh: 人们总容易积攒东西，有时自己还浑然不觉。

usage.note: to 后接动词原形，说明所采取行动的目的，但不保证成功。
usage.example: Some things are collected deliberately in the home in an attempt to avoid waste.
usage.exampleZh: 有些东西是人们为避免浪费而有意收存在家里的。

usage.note: bearing 在这里表示关联，不是轴承；some、little、no 可表示关联程度。
usage.example: This hobby educates one not only in the chosen subject, but also in general matters which have some bearing on it.
usage.exampleZh: 这种爱好不仅让人在选定的领域增长知识，也让人了解与之有关的一般知识。

usage.note: 固定搭配，notes 用复数，不一定真要交换书面笔记。
usage.example: One wants to meet like-minded collectors, to get advice, to compare notes, to exchange articles, to show off the latest find.
usage.exampleZh: 人们会想结识志趣相投的收藏者，向他们请教、交流心得、交换藏品，并炫耀最新的发现。

usage.note: circle 比喻一群有联系的人，可与 widen、grow 等表示扩大的词搭配。
usage.example: So one’s circle of friends grows.
usage.exampleZh: 于是，朋友圈也就扩大了。

usage.note: 介词短语，search 前不加冠词；不要与动词 search for 混用结构。
usage.example: Soon the hobby leads to travel, perhaps to a meeting in another town, possibly a trip abroad in search of a rare specimen, for collectors are not confined to any one country.
usage.exampleZh: 不久，这种爱好还会带来旅行：也许是去另一个城镇参加聚会，也许是出国寻觅一件稀有藏品，因为收藏者并不局限于某一个国家。

rows.en: Punctuality is a necessary habit in all public affairs in civilized society.
rows.zh: 在文明社会的一切公共事务中，守时都是必不可少的习惯。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Without it, nothing could ever be brought to a conclusion; everything would be in a state of chaos.
rows.zh: 没有它，任何事情都无法完成，一切都会陷入混乱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Only in a sparsely-populated rural community is it possible to disregard it.
rows.zh: 只有在人烟稀少的乡村社区，才可能不去理会守时。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In ordinary living, there can be some tolerance of unpunctuality.
rows.zh: 日常生活中，对不守时的情况可以有一定的宽容。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The intellectual, who is working on some abstruse problem, has everything coordinated and organized for the matter in hand.
rows.zh: 研究某个深奥问题的知识分子，已经把一切都协调、组织好，以便处理眼前的课题。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He is therefore forgiven if late for a dinner party.
rows.zh: 因此，他赴晚宴迟到了，也会得到谅解。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But people are often reproached for unpunctuality when their only fault is cutting things fine.
rows.zh: 不过，人们常因不守时而受到责备，其实唯一的过错只是把时间算得太紧。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is hard for energetic, quick-minded people to waste time, so they are often tempted to finish a job before setting out to keep an appointment.
rows.zh: 精力旺盛、头脑敏捷的人很难容忍浪费时间，因此他们常常忍不住想在动身赴约之前，再做完一件事。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If no accidents occur on the way, like punctured tyres, diversions of traffic, sudden descent of fog, they will be on time.
rows.zh: 如果路上不发生爆胎、交通改道、突起大雾等意外，他们是能准时赶到的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They are often more industrious, useful citizens than those who are never late.
rows.zh: 与那些从不迟到的人相比，他们往往是更勤奋、更有益于社会的公民。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The over-punctual can be as much a trial to others as the unpunctual.
rows.zh: 过分守时的人，给别人带来的烦恼可能和不守时的人一样多。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The guest who arrives half an hour too soon is the greatest nuisance.
rows.zh: 提前半小时到的客人最让人头疼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Some friends of my family had this irritating habit.
rows.zh: 我们家有些朋友，就有这种讨厌的习惯。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The only thing to do was ask them to come half an hour later than the other guests.
rows.zh: 唯一的办法，就是请他们比别的客人晚半小时来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Then they arrived just when we wanted them.
rows.zh: 这样，他们到达的时间，正好就是我们希望他们来的时间。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If you are catching a train, it is always better to be comfortably early than even a fraction of a minute too late.
rows.zh: 如果你要赶火车，宁可早一些、从容到站，也不要晚到哪怕不足一分钟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Although being early may mean wasting a little time, this will be less than if you miss the train and have to wait an hour or more for the next one; and you avoid the frustration of arriving at the very moment when the train is drawing out of the station and being unable to get on it.
rows.zh: 虽然早到可能意味着浪费一点时间，却总比误了火车、不得不再等一小时甚至更久才有下一班车的耗时少；而且也能避免那种沮丧：自己到站的那一刻，火车正开出车站，却怎么也上不去。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: An even harder situation is to be on the platform in good time for a train and still to see it go off without you.
rows.zh: 更难受的一种情形是，自己早已及时到达站台，却仍眼睁睁看着火车撇下自己开走。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Such an experience befell a certain young girl the first time she was travelling alone.
rows.zh: 一个年轻姑娘第一次独自旅行时，就遭遇了这样的事。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She entered the station twenty minutes before the train was due, since her parents had impressed upon her that it would be unforgivable to miss it and cause the friends with whom she was going to stay to make two journeys to meet her.
rows.zh: 她在火车预定到站前二十分钟进了车站，因为父母反复叮嘱过她，要是误车，害得她要去投宿的那家朋友跑两趟来接她，那是不可原谅的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She gave her luggage to a porter and showed him her ticket.
rows.zh: 她把行李交给一个搬运工，并把车票拿给他看。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: To her horror he said that she was two hours too soon.
rows.zh: 令她惊恐的是，他说她早到了两个小时。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She felt in her handbag for the piece of paper on which her father had written down all the details of the journey and gave it to the porter.
rows.zh: 她在手提包里摸出一张纸，上面是父亲写下的全部行程细节，然后把纸递给搬运工。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He agreed that a train did come into the station at the time on the paper and that it did stop, but only to take on mail, not passengers.
rows.zh: 他承认，确实有一班火车会在纸上写的时间进站，也确实会停车，但只装载邮件，不上旅客。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The girl asked to see a timetable, feeling sure that her father could not have made such a mistake.
rows.zh: 姑娘要求看时刻表，确信父亲不可能犯这样的错误。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The porter went to fetch one and arrived back with the station master, who produced it with a flourish and pointed out a microscopic ‘o’ beside the time of the arrival of the train at his station; this little ‘o’ indicated that the train only stopped for mail.
rows.zh: 搬运工去取时刻表，回来时站长也一同来了；站长颇有派头地拿出时刻表，指出该站火车到达时间旁有个小得几乎看不见的“o”；这个小“o”表示，火车停车只是为了装邮件。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Just at that moment the train came into the station.
rows.zh: 就在此时，火车进站了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The girl, tears streaming down her face, begged to be allowed to slip into the guard’s van.
rows.zh: 姑娘泪流满面，恳求让她悄悄上乘务员车厢。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But the station master was adamant: rules could not be broken.
rows.zh: 可站长毫不通融：规章不能破。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And she had to watch that train disappear towards her destination while she was left behind.
rows.zh: 于是，她只能看着那班火车朝自己的目的地驶去，自己却被留在了原地。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: in a state of 后接状态名词；chaos 是不可数名词。
usage.example: Without it, nothing could ever be brought to a conclusion; everything would be in a state of chaos.
usage.exampleZh: 没有它，任何事情都无法完成，一切都会陷入混乱。

usage.note: in hand 在这里表示正在办理，不是字面上拿在手里。
usage.example: The intellectual, who is working on some abstruse problem, has everything coordinated and organized for the matter in hand.
usage.exampleZh: 研究某个深奥问题的知识分子，已经把一切都协调、组织好，以便处理眼前的课题。

usage.meaning: 把时间安排得太紧；不留余地
usage.note: 常用于出门或赶期限时几乎没有缓冲时间，带有险些来不及的意味。
usage.example: But people are often reproached for unpunctuality when their only fault is cutting things fine.
usage.exampleZh: 不过，人们常因不守时而受到责备，其实唯一的过错只是把时间算得太紧。

usage.note: keep 在这里指履行约定；make an appointment 则是预约。
usage.example: It is hard for energetic, quick-minded people to waste time, so they are often tempted to finish a job before setting out to keep an appointment.
usage.exampleZh: 精力旺盛、头脑敏捷的人很难容忍浪费时间，因此他们常常忍不住想在动身赴约之前，再做完一件事。

usage.note: 表示到得足够早、不会匆忙；语气比单纯的 on time 更强调余量。
usage.example: An even harder situation is to be on the platform in good time for a train and still to see it go off without you.
usage.exampleZh: 更难受的一种情形是，自己早已及时到达站台，却仍眼睁睁看着火车撇下自己开走。

usage.note: that 后接需要牢记的内容；upon 也可换成 on。
usage.example: She entered the station twenty minutes before the train was due, since her parents had impressed upon her that it would be unforgivable to miss it and cause the friends with whom she was going to stay to make two journeys to meet her.
usage.exampleZh: 她在火车预定到站前二十分钟进了车站，因为父母反复叮嘱过她，要是误车，害得她要去投宿的那家朋友跑两趟来接她，那是不可原谅的。
